Book Building Process

Book building, in the context of the Issue, refers to the process of collection of Bids from investors on the basis of the Red
Herring Prospectus and the Bid cum Application Forms within the Price Band. The Price Band will be decided by our
Company, in consultation with the Book Running Lead Manager and if not disclosed in the Red Herring Prospectus, will
be advertised in all editions of [●], a widely circulated English national daily newspaper, all editions of [●], a widely
circulated Hindi national daily newspaper, and all editions of [●], a widely circulated Kannada daily newspaper (Kannada
being the regional language of Karnataka, where our Registered Office is located), at least two Working Days prior to the
Bid / Issue Opening Date and shall be made available to the Stock Exchange for the purposes of uploading on their
respective websites. The Issue Price shall be determined by our Company, in consultation with the Book Running Lead
Manager, after the Bid / Issue Closing Date. For details, see “Issue Procedure” on page 360.

All Bidders, other than Anchor Investors, shall only participate in this Issue through the ASBA process by providing
the details of their respective ASBA Account in which the corresponding Bid Amount will be blocked by the SCSBs.
UPI Bidders shall participate through the ASBA process, either by (i) providing the details of their respective ASBA
Account in which the corresponding Bid Amount will be blocked by the SCSBs; or (ii) using the UPI Mechanism.
Non-Institutional Bidders with an application size of up to ₹5,00,000 shall use the UPI Mechanism and shall also
provide their UPI ID in the Bid cum Application Form submitted with Syndicate Members, Registered Brokers,
Collecting Depository Participants and Registrar and Share Transfer Agents. Anchor Investors are not permitted
to participate in the Issue through the ASBA process.

In accordance with the SEBI ICDR Regulations, QIBs, Non-Institutional Bidders and Individual Bidders are not
permitted to withdraw or lower the size of their Bid(s) (in terms of the quantity of the Equity Shares or the Bid
Amount) at any stage. Further, Anchor Investors in the Anchor Investor Portion cannot withdraw their Bids after
the Anchor Investor Bidding Date. Allocation to QIBs (other than Anchor Investors) will be on a proportionate basis
while allocation to Anchor Investors will be on a discretionary basis. Additionally, allotment to each Non-
Institutional Bidder shall not be less than the minimum application size, subject to the availability of Equity Shares
in the Non – Institutional Portion, and the remaining Equity Shares, if any, shall be allotted on a proportionate
basis. For an illustration of the Book Building Process and further details, see “Terms of the Issue” and “Issue
Procedure” on pages 346 and 360, respectively.




                                                               93
The Book Building Process under the SEBI ICDR Regulations and the Bidding Process are subject to change from
time to time and the investors are advised to make their own judgement about investment through this process prior
to submitting a Bid in the Issue.

Bidders should note that the Issue is also subject to obtaining final listing and trading approvals from the Stock Exchange,
which our Company shall apply for after Allotment within two Working Days of the Bid / Issue Closing Date or such other
time period as may be prescribed under applicable law.

For further details on the method and procedure for Bidding, see “Issue Procedure” on page 360.

     Pursuant to BSE Circular no. 20190718-28 dated July 18, 2019, the Market Maker shall confirm that it has sufficient net
     worth to enable them to discharge their respective market making obligations in full.

     The Market Maker shall at all times adhere to the byelaws, rules and regulations of BSE and shall comply with such
     operational parameters, rulings, notices, guidelines and instructions of BSE as may be applicable from time to time. The
     Market Maker shall also comply with the SEBI ICDR Regulations, circulars issued by SEBI from time to time and such
     other rules, regulations and or guidelines issued by SEBI from time to time.

     Following is a summary of the key details pertaining to the Market Making arrangement:

1.   The Market Maker shall provide eligible 2-way quotes for 75% of the market time for each trading session of the normal
     market from the date of listing of the equity shares. The same shall be monitored by the BSE. Further, the Market Maker
     shall inform BSE in advance for each and every black out period when the quotes are not being issued by the Market Maker.

2.   The minimum depth of the quote shall be ₹1,00,000. However, the Bidders with holdings of value less than ₹1,00,000 shall
     be allowed to issue their holding to the Market Maker in that scrip provided that they sell their entire holding in that scrip
     in one lot along with a declaration to the effect to the selling broker. Based on the IPO price of ₹ [●]/- per equity share, the
     minimum lot size is [●] Equity Shares, thus minimum depth of the quote shall be ₹ [●] until the same would be revised by
     BSE.

3.   After first three (3) months of the market making period, the Market Maker would be exempted to provide quote if the
     Equity Shares of the Market Maker in our company reaches to 20% of the issue size (including [●] Equity Shares ought to
     be allotted under this Issue). Any Equity Shares allotted to Market Maker under this Issue over and above [●] Equity Shares
     would not be taken into consideration of computing the threshold of 20% of the issue size. As soon as the Equity Shares of
     the Market Maker in our Company reduces to 19%, the Market Maker will resume providing 2-way quotes.

4.   There shall be no exemption/threshold on downside. However, in the event the Market Maker exhausts its inventory through
     market making process, BSE may intimate the same to SEBI after due verification.

5.   On the first day of the listing, there will be a pre-opening session (call auction) for a duration of 60 minutes i.e. from 9:00
     a.m. to 10:00 a.m., out of which 45 minutes shall be allowed for order entry, order modification and order cancellation, 10
     minutes for order matching and trade confirmation and the remaining 5 minutes shall be the buffer period to facilitate the
     transition from pre-open session to the normal trading session. The circuits will apply from the first day of the listing on
     the discovered price during the pre-open call auction. The equity shares of the company would remain in Trade for Trade
     segment for 10 days from the date of listing of Equity shares on BSE.

6.   Pursuant to SEBI Circular no. CIR/MRD/DP/ 02/2012 dated January 20, 2012 and BSE Circular no. 20141201-18 dated
     December 01, 2014, the applicable price bands for the first day for Issue size up to ₹250 Crores shall be:

     a.   In case equilibrium price is discovered in the Call Auction, the price band in the normal trading session shall be 5%
          of the equilibrium price;

     b.   In case equilibrium price is not discovered in the Call Auction, the price band in the normal trading session shall be
          5% of the Issue price.

     Further, the following spread will be applicable on the BSE SME:

      Sr. No.        Market Price Slab (in Rs.)                                            Proposed spread (in % to sale price)
           1.        Up to 50                                                              9%
           2.        50 to 75                                                              8%
           3.        75 to 100                                                             6%
           4.        Above 100                                                             5%

7.   Execution of the order at the quoted price and quantity must be guaranteed by the Market Maker, for the quotes given by
     them.



                                                                   96
8.   During the compulsory market making period, the Market Maker shall not buy equity shares from the promoters or any
     persons belonging to the promoter group or any person who has acquired equity shares from such promoters or promoter
     group.

9.   There would not be more than five (5) Market Makers for the company’s Equity Shares at any point of time and the Market
     Makers may compete with other Market Makers for better quotes to the Bidders. At this stage, [●] is acting as the sole
     Market Maker.

10. The shares of the company will be traded in continuous trading session from the time and day the company gets listed on
    BSE SME and market maker will remain present as per the guidelines mentioned under BSE and SEBI circulars.

11. There will be special circumstances under which the Market Maker may be allowed to withdraw temporarily/fully from the
    market for instance due to system problems, any other problems. All controllable reasons require prior approval from BSE,
    while no prior approval for non-controllable reasons. The decision of the BSE for deciding controllable and non-
    controllable reasons would be final.

12. The Market Maker shall have the right to terminate said arrangement by giving one month notice or on mutually acceptable
    terms to the Book Running Lead Manager, who shall then be responsible to appoint a new Market Maker.

     In case of termination of the abovementioned Market Making Agreement prior to the completion of the compulsory Market
     Making period, it shall be the responsibility of the Book Running Lead Manager to arrange for another Market Maker(s) in
     replacement during the term of the notice period being served by the Market Maker but prior to the date of releasing the
     existing Market Maker from its duties in order to ensure compliance with the requirements of Regulation 261 of the SEBI
     ICDR Regulations. Further, the Company and the Book Running Lead Manager reserve the right to appoint other Market
     Maker(s) either as a replacement of the current Market Maker or as an additional Market Maker subject to the total number
     of Designated Market Makers does not exceed five (5) or as specified by the relevant laws and regulations applicable at
     that particular point of time.

13. BSE SME will have all the margins which are applicable on the BSE Main Board viz., Mark-to-Market, Value-At-Risk
    (VAR) Margin, Extreme Loss Margin, Special Margins and Base Minimum Capital etc. BSE can impose any other margins
    as deemed necessary from time-to-time.

14. BSE will monitor the obligations on a real time basis and punitive action will be initiated for any exceptions and / or non-
    compliances. Penalties / fines may be imposed by the BSE on the Market Maker; in case they are not able to provide the
    desired liquidity in a particular security as per the specified guidelines. These penalties / fines are set by the BSE from time
    to time. BSE will impose a penalty on the Market Maker in case they are not present in the market (issuing two-way quotes)
    for at least 75% of the time. The nature of the penalty will be monetary as well as suspension in market making activities /
    trading membership. The Department of Surveillance and Supervision of the BSE would decide and publish the penalties /
    fines / suspension for any type of misconduct / manipulation / other irregularities by the Market Maker from time to time.

15. All the above-mentioned conditions and systems regarding the Market Making Arrangement are subject to change based
    on changes or additional regulations and guidelines from SEBI and BSE from time to time.

7.   Promoters’ Contribution and Lock-in

     (i) Details of minimum Promoters’ contribution locked in for three years or any other period as may be prescribed
         under applicable law

     Pursuant to the Regulation 236 and 238 of the SEBI ICDR Regulations, an aggregate of at least 20.00% of the post issue
     equity share capital of our Company held by our Promoters shall be considered as minimum promoters’ contribution and
     locked-in for a period of three years from the date of allotment in this Issue. Further (i) fifty percent of promoters holding
     in excess of minimum promoters’ contribution shall be locked in for a period of two years from the date of allotment in this
     Issue; and (ii) remaining fifty percent. of promoters’ holding in excess of minimum promoters’ contribution shall be locked
     in for a period of one year from the date of allotment in this Issue.

     As on date of this Draft Red Herring Prospectus, our Promoters hold 1,21,40,000 equity shares constituting 82.09% of the
     issued, subscribed and paid-up equity share capital of our Company.

     Our Promoters have given consent to include such number of Equity Shares held by them, in aggregate, as may constitute
     20.00% of the post issue Equity Share capital of our Company as Promoters’ Contribution.

     Further, since the post Issue shareholding of our promoters is more than 20.00%, alternative investment funds or foreign
     venture capital investors or scheduled commercial banks or public financial institutions or insurance companies registered
     with Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India or any non-individual public shareholder holding at least
     5.00% of the post Issue capital or any entity (individual or non-individual) forming part of our promoter group other than
     the promoter(s), do not require to contribute to meet the shortfall in minimum Promoters’ contribution as specified in the
     SEBI ICDR Regulations.

     Our Promoters have agreed not to dispose, sell, transfer, charge, pledge or otherwise encumber in any manner, the Equity
     Shares which will be locked-in for minimum Promoters’ Contribution from the date of this Draft Red Herring Prospectus,
     until the expiry of the lock-in period specified above, or for such other time as required under SEBI ICDR Regulations,
     except as may be permitted, in accordance with the SEBI ICDR Regulations.

     The details of Equity Shares held by our Promoters, which will be locked in for minimum Promoters’ Contribution for a
     period of three years, from the date of Allotment as Promoters’ Contribution are as provided below:

(ii) Details of share capital locked-in for one year or any other period as may be prescribed under applicable law

In terms of Regulation 239 of the SEBI ICDR Regulations, the entire pre-issue equity share capital of our Company will
be locked-in for a period of one year from the date of allotment in this Issue except for:

 (a) Equity Shares allotted to employees, whether currently an employee or not, under an employee stock option or
     employee stock purchase scheme or a stock appreciation right scheme of our company prior to the initial public offer;

 (b) Equity Shares held by an employee stock option trust or transferred to the employees by an employee stock option
     trust pursuant to exercise of options by the employees, whether currently employees or not, in accordance with the
     employee stock option plan or employee stock purchase scheme or a stock appreciation right scheme;

     Provided that the equity shares allotted to the employees shall be subject to the provisions of lock-in as specified under
     the Securities and Exchange Board of India (Share Based Employee Benefits and Sweat Equity) Regulations, 2021;

 (c) Any equity shares held by a VCF or Category I AIF or Category II AIF or FVCI (as defined under the SEBI FVCI
     Regulations), as applicable, provided that such Equity Shares shall be locked in for a period of at least one year
     prescribed under the SEBI ICDR Regulations from the date of purchase by such shareholders, and such VCF or
     Category I AIF or Category II AIF or a FVCI holds, individually or with persons acting in concert, less than 20% of
     pre-issue Equity Share capital of the Company.

(iii) Lock-in of Equity Shares Allotted to Anchor Investors

50% of the Equity Shares allotted to Anchor Investors under the Anchor Investor Portion shall be locked-in for a period of
90 days from the date of Allotment and the remaining 50% shall be locked-in for a period of 30 days from the date of
Allotment.


                                                             106
     (iv) Other details with respect to lock-in, pledge and transferability

     As on the date of this Draft Red Herring Prospectus, none of our Equity Shares are held by any VCF or Category I AIF or
     Category II AIF or FVCI. As required under Regulation 241 of the SEBI ICDR Regulations, our Company shall ensure
     that the details of the Equity Shares locked-in are recorded by the relevant Depository.

     In terms of Regulation 243 of the SEBI ICDR Regulations, Equity Shares held by our Promoters which are locked in, may
     be transferred to Promoters or members of the Promoter Group or to any new Promoter, subject to continuation of lock-in
     in the hands of the transferees for the remaining period and compliance with provisions of the SEBI SAST Regulations, as
     applicable and such transferee shall not be eligible to transfer them till the lock-in period stipulated in SEBI ICDR
     Regulations has expired. The Equity Shares held by persons other than our Promoters and locked-in for a period of one
     year from the date of Allotment in the Issue, may be transferred to any other person holding Equity Shares which are locked
     -in, subject to the continuation of the lock-in in the hands of the transferee for the remaining period and compliance with
     the provisions of the SEBI SAST Regulations.

     In terms of Regulation 242 of the SEBI ICDR Regulations, the Equity Shares held by our Promoters which are locked-in
     as per Regulation 238 of the SEBI ICDR Regulations, may be pledged only with scheduled commercial banks or public
     financial institutions or systemically important non-banking finance companies or housing finance companies as collateral
     security for loans granted by such entity, provided that if the equity shares are locked-in in terms of clause (a) of Regulation
     238, the loan has been granted to the our company for the purpose of financing one or more of the Objects of the Issue and
     pledge of specified securities is one of the terms of sanction of the loan; or if the equity shares are locked-in in terms of
     clause (b) of Regulation 238 and the pledge of specified securities is one of the terms of sanction of the loan. However,
     such lock-in will continue pursuant to any invocation of the pledge and the transferee of the Equity Shares pursuant to such
     invocation shall not be eligible to transfer the Equity Shares until the expiry of the lock-in period stipulated above.

     preferential or otherwise after the date of the listing of equity shares to finance an acquisition, merger or joint venture or
     for regulatory compliance or such other scheme of arrangement or any other purpose as the Board may deem fit, if an
     opportunity of such nature is determined by its Board of Directors to be in the interest of our Company.

   Details of the Objects

1. Funding capital expenditure for the acquisition of a property comprising land and an existing building, proposed
   to be utilized for establishing and operating a new manufacturing facility and corporate office




                                                                                                 112
Our Company currently operates one registered office, one manufacturing facility comprising two sheds, and a warehouse
located in Mysore, Karnataka. The existing manufacturing facility undertakes the assembly, wiring, and testing of HT/LT
electrical panels, control and relay panels, compact substations, and related systems, primarily serving our EPC operations
in railway electrification, power distribution, and industrial infrastructure sectors.

To support our growing business operations and enhance our in-house production capabilities, our Company proposes to
utilize ₹412.00 lakhs from the Net Proceeds of the Issue in Fiscal 2027 towards funding the capital expenditure for the
acquisition of a property comprising land and an existing industrial building. The proposed property, situated at Industrial
Plot No. Q-140, Industrial Estate, Hebbal, Mysore – 570 816, Karnataka, India is intended to serve as an integrated
manufacturing facility as well as the corporate office of our Company. As our current registered office is operated from a
rented premises, the acquisition of this property will also enable the Company to establish a self-owned, permanent
registered and corporate office in the future.




The said land and existing industrial building will be purchased from M/s. P.S. Electricals pursuant to an Agreement to
Sale dated October 20, 2025, for a total consideration of ₹412.00 lakhs. An advance payment of ₹30.00 lakhs has already
been made from internal accruals on October 30, 2025, and the balance amount, will be funded from the Net Proceeds of
the Issue. The proposed property is strategically located within an industrial estate, offering proximity to our current
operations, availability of skilled manpower, reliable utilities, and logistical advantages for material sourcing and dispatch.
The acquisition will also enable us to shift from rented premises to a self-owned, permanent registered and corporate
office, thereby providing operational stability and reducing long-term rental and relocation costs.

Prior to the proposed acquisition, we have undertaken necessary due diligence and obtained requisite documentation from
the previous owner, including the sanctioned building plan, deed of sale, khata certificate, possession certificate, and latest
property tax receipt. Further, our Company has conducted an independent valuation of the property and has filed an
application to verify the encumbrance status of the property. The proposed facility has adequate space and layout for
future expansion and integration of automation systems, thereby supporting long-term scalability.

Our Company confirms that no external borrowings are proposed to be utilized for this object, and based on current
estimates, no identifiable cost overruns are anticipated. The investment aligns with our strategic objective of consolidating
operations, improving production efficiency, and reducing dependency on third-party facilities. The new facility is
expected to serve as our unit for panel manufacturing and assembly, integrating design, production, testing, and
administrative functions under one roof. The Board of Directors, through its resolution dated November 17, 2025, has
approved the proposed acquisition, and an internal monitoring mechanism will oversee the timely completion of the
project within the stipulated implementation period.

The acquisition of the new property is for:

•   Establishing a dedicated, consolidated, and fully integrated manufacturing unit and office space for our company;
•   Expanding our production and testing capacity to meet the increasing demand from EPC projects across power,
    railway, and industrial sectors;
•   Strengthening our operational control, brand visibility, and compliance readiness by operating from a self-owned,
    strategically located facility; and
•   Ensuring long-term stability by transitioning from rented premises to a permanent, company-owned registered and
    corporate office, thereby reducing rental dependency and relocation risks.

(a) Key Features and Benefits of the Proposed Facility

The proposed investment in the facility is intended to have the following objectives and benefits:

                                                             113
Strengthening SCADA, RTU and IoT Assembly & Integration Capabilities: SCADA and Automation constitute one of
our Company’s core business verticals and involve deployment of specialised hardware such as Remote Terminal Units
(RTUs), IoT gateways, edge controllers, communication modules, and field-level automation devices. The proposed
facility will house an in-house manufacturing, configuration, and testing centre for these systems. This backward
integration will enable:

  •    Greater control over component quality, firmware loading, calibration, and acceptance testing;
  •    Standardisation of hardware deployed across turnkey projects;
  •    Reduction in dependency on third-party assemblers and OEMs; and
  •    Improved reliability, lifecycle management, and field maintainability.

This capability addition is expected to significantly enhance technical robustness and execution quality in utility and
industrial automation projects.

Enhanced Operational Efficiency Through Consolidation of Functions: The facility will accommodate both our
Company’s corporate office and its hardware assembly/production operations. Operating from a single, integrated location
will ensure:

  •    Faster coordination between design, engineering, procurement, production, QA/QC, accounts, and administrative
       teams;
  •    Seamless inter-departmental communication and improved project planning;
  •    Reduced inter-location logistics, material movement, and administrative overheads; and
  •    Faster project execution cycles and quicker customer turnaround.

As the facility is ready-to-move, we will be able to commence operations immediately and efficiently deploy IPO proceeds
without construction delays.

Increased Production and Testing Capacity with Scalability: The proposed premises will provide adequate infrastructure
for setting up an expanded assembly and testing environment for SCADA panels, RTUs, IoT devices, and related
automation hardware. Key advantages include:

  •    Support for higher production capacity aligned with project inflow;
  •    Faster FAT (Factory Acceptance Test) cycles and improved testing automation;
  •    Ability to undertake large batch production for utilities and railways;
  •    Flexibility for customised, project-specific hardware configuration; and
  •    Infrastructure readiness to scale operations in line with smart grid, smart city, railway electrification, and industrial
       automation demand.

Long-Term Financial Benefits and Cost Optimisation: The acquisition of a self-owned premises is expected to deliver
significant long-term financial advantages:

  •    Elimination of recurring rental expenses and multi-location overhead costs;
  •    Reduction in external fabrication/assembly and logistics expenses;
  •    Stable occupancy costs and insulation from rental escalations;
  •    Long-term asset creation and strengthening of the Company’s balance sheet; and
  •    Improved margins through better resource utilisation and operational synergies.

Support for Strategic Growth and Technology Development: The proposed investment will support our long-term strategic
initiatives, such as:

  •    Development of proprietary hardware and embedded systems;
  •    Expansion of automation solutions covering smart metering, distribution automation, and predictive analytics;
  •    Strengthening of product IP, R&D capabilities, and in-house engineering competencies; and
  •    Improved competitiveness in government and private sector tenders.

The facility will also enable us to respond to the rising demand for integrated automation solutions across utilities,
infrastructure, mobility, and industrial markets.

2. Funding incremental working capital requirements

   We are an Engineering, Procurement, Construction and Commissioning company engaged in providing integrated
   infrastructure and engineering solutions across the power distribution, water and wastewater, automation, and utility
   infrastructure sectors. Our expertise spans the entire project lifecycle which involves design, engineering, procurement,
   erection, testing, commissioning, and operation & maintenance. We also operate an in-house manufacturing facility for
   High-Tension and Low-Tension electrical panels and compact substations, enabling us to offer customized, reliable, and
   cost-efficient products that complement our EPCC activities. Our company also undertakes sub-contracting assignments,
   providing on-ground execution support for a wide range of engineering projects.

   India’s EPC industry delivers services including design and engineering, procurement, civil works, installation,
   commissioning and operation and maintenance covering Railway EPC, Drinking Water & Wastewater Treatment, Power
   Distribution Panels and Compact Substation, Transmission and Distribution and SCADA and Automation. India’s
   Railway EPC market grew from INR 16.2 thousand crore in FY 20 to INR 30.4 thousand crore in FY 25 and is expected
   to reach INR 50.5 thousand crore by FY 30F. The drinking water and wastewater market is projected to reach INR 169.6
   thousand crore by FY 30F, supported by growth across panels, transmission and distribution and SCADA segments.
   Indian Infrastructure EPC Market is defined as the total domestic revenue generated from engineering, procurement, and
   construction (EPC) activities undertaken within India across Railway Infrastructure and Water Infrastructure segments,
   along with the related markets for HT/LT Power Distribution Panels, Compact Substations (CSS), and SCADA &
   Automation Systems. (Source: Ken Report). We intend to capitalize on the growing opportunities in the electrical
   infrastructure and EPC industry, leveraging our established customer base, execution track record, and experienced
   management team.

   Our working capital cycle primarily comprises project-based receivables, inventory, and contract advances. Historically,
   we have financed these requirements through a mix of bank borrowings, unsecured loans, and internal accruals. Given
   the growth in operations and increased project volume, we require additional funds to meet our incremental working
   capital requirements, including placement of fixed deposits for the sanction and utilization of non-fund-based facilities
   such as Bank Guarantees (BGs) and Letters of Credit (LCs). Strengthening our working capital base will enhance liquidity,
   enable timely procurement of materials, and ensure seamless execution of large-scale projects.

   The proposed deployment of funds is expected to facilitate:

   •     Timely execution of existing and new EPC contracts;


                                                                115
•        Improved credit standing for securing non-fund-based banking facilities; and
•        Unlocking of internal accruals presently tied up in the working capital cycle.

Our working capital requirements are influenced by several operational and financial factors inherent to the nature of our
EPC and manufacturing business. The key determinants include:

Project Execution Cycle and Billing Milestones: Our business follows a milestone-based billing system, where receivables
are recognized progressively upon completion of design, supply, installation, testing, and commissioning stages. The
timing gap between project execution and milestone certification directly affects receivable levels and short-term liquidity.

Credit Periods Extended to Clients: Government departments, PSUs, and large private clients often have extended
payment cycles. Delays in certification or release of payments, especially in turnkey contracts, can lead to temporary
increases in trade receivables, thereby impacting our working capital cycle.

Credit Terms with Suppliers and Subcontractors: We procure raw materials such as conductors, switchgear components,
and fabricated structures from approved vendors on credit terms that vary based on the supplier relationship and market
conditions. Any tightening of supplier credit terms or increased procurement costs can elevate working capital
requirements.

Inventory Levels for Ongoing Projects: We maintain inventory of electrical components, sheet metal, switchgear items,
and other consumables to ensure uninterrupted execution of EPC projects. The need to maintain buffer stock for time-
bound railway and infrastructure projects also affects the working capital outlay.

Mobilization Advances and Retention Money: While we receive mobilization advances from clients for project
commencement, these are typically adjusted against future billing milestones. Additionally, retention money withheld by
clients until defect-liability completion affects cash inflows and liquidity.

Bank Guarantee and Letter of Credit Margins: Our projects require performance bank guarantees, security deposits, and
LCs for procurement of imported and domestic components. The margin money or fixed deposits placed with banks for
these non-fund-based limits influence our overall working capital deployment.

Project Mix and Seasonality of Execution: The proportion of projects under execution (railway electrification, SCADA
automation, water and wastewater management, etc.) and their respective material intensity determine the level of current
asset investment. Project execution pace may vary depending on client approvals, site access, and monsoon conditions.

Operational Scale and New Order Book: As we expand our order book and undertake larger EPC contracts, the
corresponding requirement for materials, manpower, subcontracting, and advance expenses increases proportionately,
thereby elevating our working capital needs.

Collections and Cash Conversion Efficiency: Our ability to monitor collections effectively, enforce payment schedules,
and manage advances and deposits from clients impacts the net working capital cycle and internal cash generation
capacity.

 (d) Justifications for holding period levels

  S. No.                                       Particulars
  Current Assets
  Inventory                                    The inventory holding period stood at 83 days in FY2023, improving to 65 days in FY2024
                                               as we optimized procurement cycles and improved supply chain coordination. In FY2025,
                                               the inventory holding period increased to 157 days, primarily attributable to the execution
                                               of larger EPC contracts requiring advance procurement of critical materials and equipment
                                               to mitigate supply chain uncertainties and ensure uninterrupted project execution.

                                               As of September 2025 (FY2026), inventory days moderated to 67 days, reflecting
                                               improved inventory planning and material consumption aligned with project milestones.
                                               Based on current order book execution schedules and procurement strategies, we expect
                                               inventory days to remain in the range of 70 days by FY2026 year-end, indicating continued
                                               strengthening of working capital efficiency.

                                               Looking ahead, the inventory holding period is projected at 80 days in FY2027, which
                                               remains within the normal operating range for engineering and construction companies
                                               where procurement is often synchronized with project timelines rather than sales cycles.

                                               The projected increase to 91 days in FY2028 is primarily strategic and linked to the
                                               anticipated execution of larger and longer-duration EPC contracts. Such projects typically
                                               require bulk procurement and advance stocking of specialized materials and equipment,
                                               which may temporarily increase inventory holding periods but enables us to secure supply



                                                                                               118
S. No.              Particulars
                    of long-lead items, mitigate price volatility in raw materials, and ensure timely completion
                    of large infrastructure projects.

                    Industry studies indicate that construction and engineering companies typically operate
                    with inventory cycles in the 60–120-day range depending on project scale, with higher
                    inventory levels often reflecting procurement for large projects rather than inefficiencies
                    in working capital management.

                    Accordingly, our inventory profile reflects project-based procurement practices common
                    in the EPCC sector, and fluctuations in inventory days are primarily linked to project mix,
                    order book size, and timing of material procurement, rather than structural inefficiencies.

                    Overall, we continue to focus on efficient inventory planning, vendor integration, and
                    milestone-based procurement strategies, which are expected to support optimal working
                    capital utilization while enabling us to execute large-scale EPC projects efficiently.
Trade Receivables   Our trade receivable cycle reflects the project-based billing structure and payment
                    mechanisms typical of the Engineering, Procurement, Construction and Commissioning
                    (EPCC) industry, where payments are linked to milestone completion, Measurement
                    certification by project In-charge, Audit by Finance dept, and in certain cases retention
                    clauses.

                    Our average trade receivable period was 55 days in FY2023 and improved to 49 days in
                    FY2024, reflecting efficient collection mechanisms and timely billing against completed
                    project milestones. Also, the average project size was roughly below Rs. 1.5 crores during
                    these FY.

                    In FY2025, trade receivable days increased to 238 days, primarily attributable to the
                    execution of larger EPC contracts with extended milestone certification timelines and
                    higher exposure to government and large infrastructure clients such as Railway,
                    KUWSDB, where payment cycles are typically longer due to multi-layered approval
                    processes, retention amounts, and progress-based billing structures. As of September 30,
                    2025, trade receivable days stood at 149 days, reflecting the continuation of these large-
                    value projects nearing certification and payment realization.

                    Based on current project execution schedules and expected milestone billing collections,
                    we expect the receivable cycle to improve to approximately 125 days by FY2026,
                    indicating normalization of working capital as pending certifications and receivables from
                    major projects are realized.

                    Looking ahead, trade receivable days are projected to remain broadly stable at 128 days in
                    FY2027 and 137 days in FY2028, which we believe is consistent with the nature of EPC
                    contracts involving large infrastructure projects with extended billing and collection cycles.

                    Industry benchmarking indicates that engineering and construction companies often
                    operate with significantly longer receivable cycles compared to other sectors, with studies
                    indicating average receivable periods of around 159 days for engineering and construction
                    companies globally, reflecting the milestone-based nature of payments and retention
                    provisions common in large infrastructure contracts.

                    Further, in construction and EPC contracting, payment collection periods are often
                    extended due to progress billing structures, certification requirements, and retention
                    holdbacks, which can lengthen the cash realization cycle despite timely project execution.

                    Accordingly, the fluctuations in our trade receivable days are primarily driven by project
                    mix, client profile (including government and large infrastructure entities), milestone
                    billing structures, and retention mechanisms, rather than structural inefficiencies in credit
                    management.

                    Our Company continues to focus on strengthening its receivable management through -
                    milestone-linked invoicing and contract structuring, regular follow-up with project


                                                  119
  S. No.                                         Particulars
                                                 authorities for certification and payment realization, and prudent selection of clients with
                                                 established payment track records.

                                                 Our management believes that these measures, together with our strong order book and
                                                 execution capabilities, will support sustainable working capital management while
                                                 enabling us to participate in large-scale infrastructure and EPC projects.
  Current Liabilities
  Trade Payables                                 Our trade payable period was 4 days in FY2023, reflecting relatively smaller procurement
                                                 volumes and advance payments to certain vendors during early project phases.

                                                 In FY 2024, trade payable days increased to 27 days, primarily due to us entering into
                                                 larger EPC contracts and negotiating extended credit terms with suppliers and
                                                 subcontractors. Such credit arrangements are common in the EPC industry, allowing
                                                 contractors to align procurement payments with project cash flows.

                                                 In FY2025, trade payable days stood at 66 days, reflecting continued utilization of supplier
                                                 credit while maintaining strong relationships with vendors and subcontractors.

                                                 As of September 2025 (FY2026), trade payable days were 39 days, and are expected to
                                                 moderate to approximately 42 days by March 2026 as certain vendor obligations are settled
                                                 upon completion of procurement cycles.

                                                 Looking forward, trade payable days are expected to normalize at approximately 87 days
                                                 in FY2027 and 104 days in FY2028, consistent with the anticipated scale of procurement
                                                 associated with future projects.

 (e) Rationale for incremental working capital requirements

Our company has estimated the working capital requirements (“WCR”) as follows:

The WCR for Fiscal 2027, WCR will increase by 134.10% as compared to Fiscal 2026, which will be in line with the
increase in sales of our Company.

Our company has estimated the working capital requirements for the financial year 2026-27 on basis of following main
assumptions:

 1.      Expansion of business

The proceeds from the Issue proposed to be utilised towards funding the incremental working capital requirements of our
Company are expected to support the expansion of our Engineering, Procurement, Construction and Commissioning
(“EPCC”) operations. A portion of the funds will be utilised as margin money and deposits required for the sanctioning
and enhancement of bank guarantees (“BGs”), letters of credit (“LCs”) and other non-fund-based credit facilities with
banks and financial institutions. These facilities are essential for bidding, securing, and executing EPCC contracts and for
meeting contractual performance and security obligations. Strengthening our BG and LC limits is expected to enable us
to participate in larger and more complex infrastructure projects and improve our credibility with clients, suppliers and
lenders.

Further, the funds will also be utilised towards the procurement of raw materials, equipment and subcontracted services
required for the execution of ongoing and proposed EPCC projects. Timely availability of working capital is expected to
facilitate uninterrupted project execution by enabling timely procurement of materials and services, improving
procurement efficiency through timely vendor payments and bulk purchasing, and reducing the risk of execution delays


                                                                                                120
arising from liquidity constraints. This is expected to support the scaling up of our project execution capabilities without
a proportionate increase in external debt.

Our operations typically involve an average billing and collection cycle of approximately 125 days, which results in
working capital being locked in receivables and project execution costs. The proposed funding of incremental working
capital requirements is expected to strengthen our liquidity position and operating efficiency by supporting smoother
project execution, timely procurement and faster billing cycles, which may reduce the effective cash conversion cycle.
Improved working capital availability may also reduce our reliance on short-term borrowings, lower interest costs and
enhance overall financial flexibility.

Accordingly, the proposed utilisation of Issue proceeds towards incremental working capital requirements is expected to
strengthen our ability to execute multiple projects concurrently, participate in higher-value infrastructure contracts and
support the overall expansion of our business operations.

procurement delays, and manage supply chain requirements more efficiently. Further, timely procurement may help
mitigate the impact of price fluctuations in key raw materials and electrical components, thereby supporting better cost
management and improved project execution margins.

The WCR will increase by ₹5,738.64 Lakhs in Fiscal 2027 out of which ₹6,000.00 Lakhs is increasing due to trade
receivables. The increase in trade receivables is expected to be in line with the anticipated growth in our revenue from
EPCC projects across the railway infrastructure, power transmission and distribution, and water and wastewater treatment
sectors. In the EPCC business model, payments from clients are typically received in stages based on project milestones,
certification of work completed, and contractual credit terms. As our project execution volume and order inflow increases,
the value of work completed and billed during the year is expected to rise correspondingly, resulting in higher outstanding
receivables during the project cycle.

Additionally, infrastructure and government-related projects generally involve defined billing milestones, verification
procedures, and approval processes before payments are released, which can extend the receivable cycle. Consequently,
as we undertake a larger number of projects and execute higher-value contracts, the level of receivables is expected to
increase proportionately. The projected increase in trade receivables therefore reflects the scale-up of our operations and
expansion of our project portfolio. Adequate working capital support is expected to enable the Company to manage this
receivable cycle efficiently, maintain liquidity for project execution, and continue to undertake multiple projects
concurrently without disruption to operations.

   Company, including administration, insurance, marketing, repairs and maintenance, payment of taxes and duties, and

   utilisation of funds towards each of the above purposes will be determined by our Board, based on the amount available

Monitoring of utilization of funds

As this is an Issue for less than ₹5,000 lakhs, we are not required to appoint a monitoring agency for the purpose of the
Issue in terms of the SEBI ICDR Regulations. However, pursuant to Regulation 262 (5) of the SEBI ICDR Regulations,
we shall submit a certificate of the statutory auditor for utilization of issue proceeds to BSE SME while filing the quarterly
financial results, till the issue proceeds are fully utilized. Further, pursuant to Regulation 262 (6) of the SEBI ICDR
Regulations, since funding the incremental working capital requirements is the Objects of the Issue and the amount raised
for the said object exceeds ₹500.00 lakhs, we shall submit a certificate of the statutory auditor to BSE SME while filing
the quarterly or half yearly financial results, for use of funds as working capital in the same format as disclosed in the
Offer Document, till the proceeds raised for the said object are fully utilized.

Our Board and Audit committee shall monitor the utilization of the net proceeds of the Issue. Our Company will disclose
the utilization of the Net Proceeds under a separate head in our balance sheet along with the relevant details, for all such
amounts that have not been utilized. Our Company will indicate investments, if any, of unutilized Net Proceeds in the
balance sheet of our Company for the relevant financial years subsequent to the completion of the Issue.

Pursuant to SEBI LODR Regulations, our Company shall disclose to the Audit Committee of the Board of Directors, the
uses and applications of the Net Proceeds. Our Company shall prepare a statement of funds utilized for purposes other
than those stated in this Draft Red Herring Prospectus and place it before the Audit Committee of the Board of Directors,
as required under applicable law. Such disclosure shall be made only until such time that all the Net Proceeds have been
utilized in full. The statement shall be certified by the statutory auditor of our Company. Furthermore, in accordance with
the Regulation 32 of the SEBI LODR Regulations, our Company shall furnish to the Stock Exchange on a half yearly
basis, a statement indicating (i) deviations, if any, in the utilization of the proceeds of the Issue from the Objects; and (ii)
details of category wise variations in the utilization of the proceeds from the Issue from the Objects. This information will
also be published in newspapers simultaneously with the interim or annual financial results, after placing the same before
the Audit Committee of the Board of Directors.

Interim Use of Funds

The Net Proceeds shall be retained in the Public Issue Account until receipt of the listing and trading approvals from the
Stock Exchange by our Company. Pending utilization of the Net Proceeds for the purposes described above, our Company
undertakes to deposit the Net Proceeds only in one or more scheduled commercial banks included in the Second Schedule
of the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934, as amended, as may be approved by our Board.

In accordance with Section 27 of the Companies Act, 2013, our Company confirms that it shall not use the Net Proceeds
for buying, trading or otherwise dealing in shares of any other listed company or for any investment in the equity markets.

Variation in Objects

In accordance with Sections 13(8) and 27 of the Companies Act, 2013 and applicable rules, and Regulation 281A of the
SEBI ICDR Regulations read with Schedule XX of the SEBI ICDR Regulations, our Company shall not vary the Objects
without our Company being authorized to do so by the Shareholders by way of a special resolution. In addition, the notice
issued to the Shareholders in relation to the passing of such special resolution (the “Notice”) shall specify the prescribed
details as required under the Companies Act, 2013. The Notice shall simultaneously be published in the newspapers, one

of an assessment of market demand for the Equity Shares offered through the Book Building Process and on the basis of
the qualitative and quantitative factors as described below. The face value of the Equity Shares is ₹10/- each and the Issue
Price is [●] times the face value at the lower end of the Price Band and [●] times the face value at the higher end of the
Price Band.

Investors should also refer to “Our Business”, “Risk Factors”, “Restated Consolidated Financial Information”,
“Management’s Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations” and “Other Financial
Information” on pages 182, 32, 285, 289 and 286, respectively, to get a more informed view before making an investment
decision.

(1)     Revenue from operations is calculated as revenue from India’s Railway EPC, Drinking Water and Waste Water Treatment, Transmission and Distribution, Power Distribution Panels and
        Compact Sub-Stations and SCADA and Automation Systems Services

        Total Equity minus DTA plus DTL, Long Term Borrowings and Short-Term Borrowings.

        receivables and closing trade receivables.
(11)    Trade Payables (days) is calculated as average trade payables divided by cost of services multiplied by 365. Cost of services is calculated as cost of materials consumed plus other direct
        expenses plus changes in Inventories of Work-in-Progress. Average Trade Payables is calculated as average of opening trade payables and closing trade payables.
(12)    Working capital cycle (days) is calculated inventory days plus trade receivables days minus trade payables days.

        within a vacuum.
 (6)    PLC (Programmable Logic Controller) is an industrial control computer that automates machines and processes. RTU (Remote Terminal Unit) collects data from remote sites and transmits it
        to a control center. HMI (Human Machine Interface) is the screen or interface through which operators monitor and control systems.

1.   SPECIAL DIRECT TAX BENEFITS AVAILABLE TO THE COMPANY

     The following benefits are available to the Company while computing its total taxable income, after fulfilling conditions,
     as per the applicable provisions of the Act:

1.1. Lower Corporate tax rate under Section 115BAA of the Act

     Section 115BAA was inserted in the Act by the Taxation Laws (Amendment) Act, 2019 (‘the Amendment Act, 2019’)
     w.e.f. April 1, 2020 (Assessment Year 2020-21). Section 115BAA grants an option to a domestic company to be governed
     by the section from a particular assessment year. If a company opts for section 115BAA of the Act, it can pay corporate
     tax at a reduced rate of 22% (plus applicable surcharge and education cess).

     Section 115BAA of the Act further provides that domestic companies availing the option will not be required to pay
     Minimum Alternate Tax (‘MAT’) on their ‘book profit’ under section 115JB of the Act. However, such a company will
     no longer be eligible to avail certain specified exemptions / incentives under the Act and will also need to comply with
     certain other conditions specified in section 115BAA of the Act.

     If a company opts for section 115BAA, the tax credit (under section 115JAA), if any, which it was entitled to on account
     of MAT paid in earlier years, will no longer be available. Further, it shall not be allowed to claim set-off of any brought
     forward loss arising to it on account of additional depreciation and other specified incentives.

India’s Infrastructure EPC Market Analysis

Indian Infrastructure EPC Market is defined as the total domestic revenue generated from engineering, procurement,
and construction (EPC) activities undertaken within India across Railway Infrastructure and Water Infrastructure
segments, along with the related markets for HT/LT Power Distribution Panels, Compact Substations (CSS), and SCADA
& Automation Systems. The market is measured in value terms (INR crore), reflects only in-country EPC execution and
export revenues are excluded.

Overview Of Public and Private Infrastructure Spending in India

India’s infrastructure buildout is one of the largest globally, with public investments leading the way. Between CY17 and
CY23, Infrastructure investments about INR 67 trillion took place in India, and over INR 143 trillion is expected between
CY24 and CY30. This highlights more than a two-fold increase (Source: CRISIL). Government agencies, both central
and state, account for nearly 80% of this expenditure, underscoring the state’s dominant role in funding and executing
projects.

At the same time, private sector participation has remained a consistent and growing pillar of India’s infrastructure
strategy, particularly through PPPAC-approved projects. These projects, cleared by the Public Private Partnership
Appraisal Committee and which are eligible for central support, reflect the government’s commitment to structured private
involvement.

Public and Private expenditure combined provide a strong push for infrastructure development driven by the
Government of India is creating significant opportunities.

In railways, new lines, station redevelopment, and freight corridors are increasing requirements for EPC works
and execution capacity. Wastewater treatment is becoming integral as urban growth and regulatory standards mandate
treatment and reuse systems.

In the power sector, transmission expansion and distribution upgrades are driving the use of HT/LT distribution
panels and compact substations to support reliable delivery.

Across power, transport, and utilities, the shift toward digital monitoring and grid stability makes SCADA and
automation systems necessary for real-time control, compliance, and operational efficiency.

private-sector-driven infrastructure development. Despite fluctuations in the number of proposals each year, the consistent
capital allocation underscores a forward-looking national infrastructure strategy.

Between FY’07 and FY’26, the railway sector accounted for over INR 5.1 lakh crore in projects spanning tracks, tunnels,
bridges, and viaducts, generating large-scale requirements in civil construction, electrification, and allied EPC works.

During the same period, the water and wastewater segment saw continued investments in treatment plants, sewage
networks, and distribution systems, sustaining steady EPC demand in process engineering and long-term O&M services.

In the power sector, projects worth around INR 4.3 lakh crore in transmission and INR 28,757 crore in distribution
required EPC contractors to deliver modern grid infrastructure, with SCADA and automation systems becoming central
to project execution. These developments collectively reflected a robust EPC pipeline anchored by strong project flow in
rail infrastructure, expanding opportunities in water and wastewater, and an increasing emphasis on automation,
substations, and HT/LT electrical integration across power projects.

Value Chain Across Target Markets

Value Chain of India’s Railway EPC Market

The value chain of India’s Railway EPC projects initiates from Tendering & Bidding of EPC projects. Once the project
is commercialised the subsequent steps are initiated which include Design & Detailed Project Report (DPR), Procurement,
Civil & Mechanical, Electrical, and Plumbing (MEP) Execution, and Signalling and Telecommunication (S&T) &
Overhead Electrification (OHE) Installation, followed by Testing & Commissioning and Handover & Operation and
Maintenance (O&M).

Note: EPC refers to Engineering, Procurement, and Construction, DPR refers to Detailed Project Report, MEP refers to Mechanical, Electrical, and Plumbing, S&T refers
                      to Signaling and Telecommunication, OHE refers to Overhead Electrification and O&M refers to Operation and Maintenance



                                                                                  138
Value Chain of India’s Drinking Water & Waste Water Treatment Market




The value chain of India’s Drinking Water and Waste Water Treatment Plant projects typically:

•   Initiates from Water Testing, which includes sampling, laboratory analysis, and baseline studies for STP, ETP, and
    WTP projects.
•   Once the initial assessments are complete, the process moves to Process Design involving technology selection and
    plant-specific engineering.
•   This is followed by Civil & Electro-Mechanical Works, covering construction of civil structures, tanks, basins, and
    installation of pumps, blowers, filters, and related infrastructure.
•   Subsequent stages include Plant Installation with erection, commissioning, and system integration, SCADA
    Integration for automation and monitoring.
•   Finally, Operation & Maintenance through daily operations, upkeep, and long-term performance contracts.

                                                                                     and Data Acquisition.


Value Chain of India’s Transmission & Distribution Market

The value chain of India’s Transmission and Distribution (T&D) projects typically starts from network planning,
route/scheme finalization, and tendering of EPC packages by central utilities (POWERGRID), state transmission utilities
(STUs), discoms, and large industrial/renewable developers. Once the project is awarded, subsequent stages include
Detailed Engineering & Tower/Foundation Designs, Procurement of conductors, towers, transformers, switchgear and
protection systems, followed by Construction & Erection of transmission lines and substations, Distribution network
rollout (11 kV/33 kV), and Metering & SCADA integration. The lifecycle is completed with Testing & Commissioning,
Energization, and finally Handover for Operation & Maintenance (O&M) to the utility.

Figure 0-5: Value Chain of India’s Transmission & Distribution Market




                                                                                Source: Ken Research Analysis



                                                                                            140
Value Chain of India’s Power Distribution Panels and Compact Substation Market

The value chain of Installing High Tension (HT) / Low Tension (LT) Distribution Panels and Compact Substation
(CSS) in India:

• Begins with the Client Bill of Quantities (BOQ, which refers to document used in construction and infrastructure
  projects that lists out the materials, parts, labor, and associated costs required to execute the work), which outlines
  requirement definition, technical specifications, and tender placement.
• Once the contract is awarded, the process moves to Panel Design & Fabrication and Component Assembly, covering
  HT/LT panels, Compact Substations, Diesel Generator (DG) synchronizing panels, and Variable Frequency Drive
  (VFD) panels.
• This is followed by Testing with functional validation and certifications, Delivery with logistics coordination, and
• Final stage Site Installation & Commissioning through cabling, energization, and handover.

                                                                                    refers to Compact Substation.


Value Chain of India’s SCADA & Automation Systems Market

The value chain of SCADA and Automation Systems projects in India primarily used in water treatment and power
plants typically includes the following process flow:

 •          Requirement gathering through site surveys, process studies, and client approvals to define scope and
            automation needs.
 •          This is followed by hardware and software design, involving PLC/RTU selection, network architecture, and
            SCADA/HMI dashboards tailored to water quality, flow, and pumps in WTPs or turbines, boilers, and load
            management in power plants.
 •          Next comes PLC/RTU setup with panel assembly, wiring, instrumentation, and configuration of process logic
            such as dosing, backwashing, or turbine control.

                                                                                              141
 •         SCADA configuration then establishes servers, databases, alarms, and operator HMIs for centralized monitoring
           and control.
 •         The system is validated through Factory and Site Acceptance Tests (FAT & SAT) before moving into annual
           maintenance contracts and analytics, which enable preventive maintenance, remote monitoring, and performance
           optimization to ensure efficiency, reliability, and compliance.

India’s Railway EPC Market Analysis

The Railway EPC Market is defined as the domestic revenue generated from EPC contracting activities related to
railway electrification, signaling & telecommunication, and civil works in India. This includes electrification works such
as OHE, TSS, and PSI; signaling & telecommunication systems; and civil works including station redevelopment, bridges,
and platforms, along with associated O&M services where executed as part of EPC contracts.

Overview of India’s Railway EPC Market

India’s Railways are largely shaped by government budgets, with the capital outlay crossing INR 2.6 lakh crore in FY26
Budget Estimates, driving most investments. This sustained funding ensures a robust pipeline of projects in
electrification, signaling, and core civil infrastructure works such as stations, depots, and bridges, defining the overall
pace and scale of EPC opportunities.

The Railway EPC market covers projects grouped into 3 categories (excluding track works and locomotive
manufacturing works):

•     Civil Engineering Works: Involves building core railway infrastructure through construction of stations, yards and
      bridges, along with supporting structures such as platforms, depots, warehouses, drainage and boundary walls.
•     Electrical Engineering Works (incl. Transmission and Distribution): Provides traction and auxiliary power by
      undertaking electrification through 25 kV AC OHE, traction substations, SCADA-enabled protection, and
      distribution networks across stations and depots.
•     Signal and Telecommunication Works: Ensures safe and efficient train operations by deploying electronic/relay
      interlocking, block signalling, track circuit interfaces, and fibre/copper-based data networks.


                                                                                           142
These works are fundamental to enhancing operational efficiency, safety and service reliability in the Indian
Railways, enabling seamless passenger and freight movement.

India’ Railway EPC Market Size Analysis, FY20–FY30F

Between FY20 and FY25, the Railway EPC market increased from INR 16.2 thousand crore to INR 30.4 thousand
crore, at a CAGR of 13.4%. Growth was driven by increasing capital outlay under the National Rail Plan, the PM
Gati Shakti programme, and major projects such as the Dedicated Freight Corridors. Significant progress was also
achieved in station redevelopment, depots, bridges, and electrification with SCADA-enabled substations.

The Speed Improvement Scheme and the freight capacity push ~3,000 MT together expand Indian Railways’ EPC
pipeline—lifting speeds to 120–160 km/h which are driving major EPC demand through large-scale track, signaling,
and OHE upgrades, along with new freight terminals and logistics hubs—enhancing speed, capacity, and network
efficiency across Indian Railways.

From FY25 to FY30F, the market is expected to grow from INR 30.4 thousand crore to INR 50.5 thousand crore, at
a CAGR of 10.7%. Key drivers include conclusion of high-speed rail projects and their commissioning, electrification
of remaining lines to meet the 100% electrification goal, OHE and substation upgrades, station modernization, and
further execution of signaling programmes such as Kavach. Integration with multimodal logistics hubs under Gati
Shakti will further support EPC demand.

India’s Railway EPC Market Segmentation, FY25-FY30F

India’s Railway EPC Segmentation by Work Type, FY25-FY30F:

The Railway EPC market is concentrated in composite infrastructure works, which accounted for 51.0% of the market
in FY25 at INR 15.5 thousand crore. The growth in this segment is propelled by new line additions, rising track
density, and stronger safety and security requirements, alongside investments in station redevelopment and
passenger amenities. The segment is expected to lead, reaching INR 28.4 thousand crore by FY30F, driven by
modernization programs, urban station upgrades, and capacity expansion.

The second-largest segment is electrification of railway lines, contributing 13.8% of the market in FY25 at INR 4.2
thousand crore. Growth in this segment showing signs of saturation, due to accelerated electrification programs

                                                                                         143
undertaken between FY20 and FY25 to reduce fuel costs and promote sustainability. As the network nears complete
electrification, growth is expected to slow, with the segment projected to reach INR 5.4 thousand crore by FY30F at
a CAGR of 5.2%.

Signaling & Telecommunication (S&T) works accounted for 12.8% of the market in FY25 at INR 3.9 thousand crore.
Growth is being driven by safety programs such as Kavach and automatic block signaling, improving efficiency and
reducing collisions. The segment is projected to reach INR 6.0 thousand crore by FY30F at an 9.0% CAGR, supported
by wider adoption of digital signaling and upgrades across busy corridors.

Among the faster-growing but smaller segments, traction substations (CAGR 11.1%) and OHE works (CAGR 10.5%)
are expected to see strong growth through FY30F, driven by the ongoing need to expand and modernize traction systems
and feeder lines to support higher-capacity, fully electrified corridors.

Opportunities in India’s Railway EPC Market

India’s Railway EPC market was valued at INR 30.4 thousand crore in FY25 and is projected to reach INR 50.5
thousand crore by FY30F, growing at a CAGR of 10.7%. Opportunities for EPC players lie in the execution of
electrification, signaling, and station redevelopment works under flagship programs such as PM Gati Shakti, Amrit
Bharat Station Scheme, and Mission Electrification. These initiatives are driving large-scale modernization of railway
infrastructure, including depots, bridges, and traction substations, to enhance operational efficiency and connectivity
across corridors.

In addition, high-speed rail corridors, dedicated freight lines, and multimodal logistics hubs are creating sustained
EPC demand across civil and electrical packages. The push toward 100% rail electrification and digital signaling
integration is expanding opportunities in OHE systems, SCADA-enabled substations, and depot construction. As
Indian Railways continues to prioritize capacity expansion and asset modernization, EPC players with capabilities in
integrated design, automation, and turnkey execution are well-positioned to capture value across this growing market.

India Metro Systems EPC Market Size Analysis, FY19–FY25-FY30F

The India Metro Systems EPC Market is defined as the domestic revenue generated from EPC contracting activities
related exclusively to urban metro rail systems in India. This includes EPC execution for metro-specific civil infrastructure
(elevated and underground corridors, viaducts, stations, depots, tunnels), metro rolling-stock–independent systems such
as traction power supply, metro signaling & telecommunication systems (including CBTC), platform screen doors, depot
systems, and associated electromechanical works, along with O&M services where bundled within metro EPC contracts.

India’s metro EPC market has grown steadily from ₹15,000 crore in FY19 to an estimated ₹23,500 crore in FY25,
reflecting a CAGR of 7.8%, and is projected to reach ₹34,700 crore by FY30F, reflecting a 8.1% CAGR. This moderate
yet sustained expansion highlights consistent investments in urban transport infrastructure, driven by new corridors and
extensions across major cities such as Delhi, Mumbai, Bengaluru, Pune, and Ahmedabad.

According to the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs (MoHUA), over 990 km of metro projects have been approved
since 2014, while an additional 1,000 km is under various stages of planning and construction across 27+ cities. The
upcoming pipeline, valued at approximately ₹3 lakh crore, supports a robust EPC opportunity averaging ₹25,000–35,000
crore annually through FY30F.

This growth reflects a balanced shift toward more complex underground alignments and integrated transit systems.
However, execution challenges—land acquisition, funding delays, and rising input costs—may constrain completion
rates. Overall, India’s metro EPC market will remain a key infrastructure driver under the Vision 2047 Urban Mobility
agenda, underpinned by steady public spending and state-level project rollouts.

electromechanical works in India. India continues to face critical challenges in drinking water access and wastewater
management. To address these challenges, the government has rolled out a series of large-scale programs focused on
expanding piped water access, modernizing urban infrastructure, and promoting wastewater treatment and reuse.

EPC and O&M Market of India’s Drinking Water and Waste Water Treatment Market

India’s drinking water and wastewater treatment market is driven by two spending streams: capital expenditure
(CAPEX) for setting up plants and infrastructure, and operational expenditure (OPEX) for their upkeep.

 •        CAPEX includes core plant construction along with intake systems, pump houses, reservoirs, and pipelines,
 •        OPEX covers recurring costs of operation, maintenance, and compliance.

These translate into two commercial segments: Engineering, Procurement & Construction (EPC), reflecting CAPEX-
led demand for new assets, and Operations & Maintenance (O&M), reflecting OPEX-led lifecycle services. Together,
they provide a full view of the market, balancing cyclical construction activity with stable O&M demand.

As more opportunities open up for EPC and O&M players in the market, there exists a variation in the
opportunities available. From FY20 to FY25, India’s drinking water and wastewater treatment market was driven by
EPC spend, while O&M formed a smaller share. In FY20, EPC contributed 80% of the market, with O&M at 20%.
This trend continued through FY25, with EPC rising to 83%, supported by large-scale project rollouts under Jal
Jeevan Mission and AMRUT 2.0 growing at a CAGR of 10.1% from FY25-FY30F.

As these schemes are scheduled to conclude by FY26, a shift is expected post-implementation, with increased O&M
spend to operate and maintain commissioned assets. By FY30F, O&M is projected to rise to 21%, reflecting growing
demand for professional long-term operations reflecting a CAGR of 16.0% from FY25-FY30F.

Opportunities in India’s Water & Wastewater Treatment Market

The Indian Drinking Water and Wastewater Treatment market, valued at INR 99.9 thousand crore in FY25, is projected
to reach INR 169.6 thousand crore by FY30F, growing at a CAGR of ~11.2%. Opportunities for EPC players lie in the
design and execution of drinking water, sewage, and effluent treatment plants under flagship government programs
such as Jal Jeevan Mission, AMRUT 2.0, and Namami Gange. The expansion of municipal and industrial
infrastructure, supported by stricter environmental regulations, continues to drive EPC demand across urban and rural
India.

Rising urbanization, industrial compliance norms, and Zero Liquid Discharge (ZLD) requirements are accelerating
investments in STPs, ETPs, and reuse systems, while smart water infrastructure and SCADA-enabled O&M
contracts provide recurring opportunities for technology-driven EPC and system integration firms. With over 80%
of projects led by public sector clients, the sector offers sustained visibility and long-term engagement potential across
both capital execution and lifecycle management services.

India’s Transmission and Distribution Market Analysis

The Transmission and Distribution (T&D) Market is defined as the domestic EPC revenue generated from the design,
supply, construction, and commissioning of transmission lines, substations, and distribution networks across India. The
scope includes high-voltage (HV) and medium-voltage (MV) infrastructure supporting power evacuation, grid
interconnection, and last-mile distribution.

Overview of India’s Transmission and Distribution Market and its Market Size, FY20-FY30F

India’s power sector is transforming rapidly with rising electricity demand and large-scale renewable integration. To
strengthen grid reliability, the government has launched major initiatives to expand interregional transmission corridors,
modernize distribution networks, and promote smart metering and loss reduction. These efforts, aligned with the target
of integrating 500 GW of renewables by 2030, are driving sustained investment across the transmission and distribution
sector.

Opportunities in India’s Transmission and Distribution Market

India’s Transmission and Distribution market, valued at INR 36.0 thousand crore in FY25, is projected to reach INR

India’s Switchgear Industry, FY20-FY30F

The India Switchgear Market represents the total revenue generated from the sale of electrical switchgear used to control,
protect, and isolate power systems across transmission, distribution, and end-user installations. It products such as circuit
breakers, panels, RMUs, and gas- or air-insulated switchgear supplied by domestic and international manufacturers. The
market is measured as the value of switchgear products sold in India, expressed in INR crores.


                                                                                        152
Distribution panels represent the final assembly, within which switchgear is only one component alongside busbars,
relays, meters, and enclosures. As a result, the panel market is structurally larger and has consistently been at least
3X the size of the standalone switchgear market, reflecting the added value of integration, customization, and ancillary
equipment.

In FY20, the Indian switchgear market stood at INR 35.9 thousand crore, rising to INR 48.0 thousand crore by FY25,
at a CAGR of 6.0%. Growth during this period was steady, supported by demand from utilities and industrial projects,
although moderated by pandemic-related slowdowns.
