India’s Power Distribution Panels and Compact Substation Market Segmentation, FY25-FY30F

India’s Power Distribution Panels and Compact Substations Market Segmentation by Type of Panel,
FY25-FY30F:

India’s Power Distribution Panels and Compact Substation (CSS) market is evolving with distinct growth patterns
across segments, driven by infrastructure upgrades, industrial demand, and urban development.

The LT Panels (up to 1.1 kV) segment remains the largest, contributing 35.1% in FY25 at INR 50.7 thousand
crore and is expected to grow at a CAGR of 6.4% between FY25 and FY30F, reaching a market size of INR 69.0
thousand crore. Growth is steady, supported by residential, commercial, and real estate demand, though the segment
is maturing.

HT Panels (11–33 kV), while smaller in share at 10.3% in FY25 at INR 14.9 thousand crore, is growing the fastest,
with a CAGR of 11.0% by FY30F, reaching INR 25.1 thousand crore. Growth is led by transmission upgrades,
renewable evacuation, and state-level investments under RDSS.

Compact Substations (CSS) contribute 14.8% in FY25 at INR 21.4 thousand crore and is expected to reach INR
33.5 thousand crore by FY30F growing at a CAGR of 9.4% between FY25 and FY30F. This growth is supported
by smart cities, metro rail, and distributed solar infrastructure in space-constrained environments.

Smaller segments like Soft Starters & VFD Panels, DG Synchronizing Panels, and Busbar Extension Panels show
mixed trends. While DG panels are slowing due to grid reliability and emissions norms, automation-focused panels are
growing with the shift toward energy efficiency and intelligent distribution systems.

The market structure for HT/LT Distribution Panels and Compact Sub-Stations (CSS) is defined by the interaction
between OEMs (Original Equipment Manufacturers), Panel Integrators, and EPC (Engineering, Procurement &
Construction) Contractors. This interaction, can be seen below.

               Figure 0-20: Interaction Between OEMs, Panel Integrators, and EPC Contractors

•    OEMs focus on manufacturing the core electrical components such as circuit breakers, relays, transformers, and
     switchgear.

     o OEMs + Panel Integrators: The OEMs themselves use the manufactured components to create power
          distribution panels to offer to the customers, and because of their larger footprint offer more expensive
          aftermarket services. And the other is,

systems to meet diverse industrial and infrastructure needs.

India’s SCADA and Automation Systems Market Analysis

India’s SCADA and Automation Systems Market Overview

The SCADA & Automation Systems Market is defined as the domestic revenue generated from the design, supply,
execution, and commissioning of SCADA and automation systems across electrical networks, water and wastewater
infrastructure, power projects, and railway installations in India. The market is segmented by end-use industry (railways,
water, power distribution), scope of work (design only, execution + commissioning), and system type.

Within India’s automation landscape, SCADA is a specialized segment focused on supervisory control, monitoring,
and data acquisition across distributed assets. It is majorly used in industries where remote visibility and system
reliability are critical. SCADA systems enable centralized control of field equipment, real-time data logging, fault
detection, and performance optimization making them essential for managing complex, large-scale infrastructure. This
indicates that SCADA remains a strategic enabler for managing essential infrastructure.

SCADA and Its Integration Across Platforms

Potential transformation of Traditional SCADA with IoT Integration
Integrating IoT devices with SCADA allows real-time data acquisition from sensors, meters, and field devices. It enables
remote monitoring, predictive maintenance, process automation, and security enhancements by connecting edge
devices directly to the control system.

Examples: Siemens uses IoT-enabled SCADA for smart grids and manufacturing automation.

Potential transformation of Traditional SCADA with GIS Integration

Combines spatial visualization from Geographic Information Systems with SCADA’s real-time data to map substations,
transformers, pipelines, and feeders.

Examples: Reliance Energy is utilizing SCADA with GIS integration to capture network changes on day-to day basis.

Integration of SCADA with Cloud Dashboards

Integrating SCADA with cloud dashboards enables remote monitoring and control through web-based interfaces. It
supports scalability, advanced analytics, automated reporting, and reduced IT costs, making SCADA data accessible
anywhere. Examples: Bharat Light & Power uses SCADA integrated with Google Cloud for remote monitoring and AI
analytics of renewable energy operations, while Indian IT firms like Wipro and Tata Consultancy Services provide
cloud-based SCADA integration solutions for industrial and utility sectors.

Industry transportation SCADA and AI Analytics

Embedding AI-powered analytics into SCADA enables predictive maintenance, anomaly detection, root cause analysis,
and process optimization. AI models analyze historical and real-time SCADA data to provide decision support and
performance optimization.

India’s Railway EPC Market

Increased Government Budget Pushing for Railway Network Expansion

The capital outlay supports critical areas such as increase in track length, S&T. In parallel, Ministry of Railways also
plans to invest INR 16.7 lakh crore by 2031 toward freight corridors, electrification, high-speed rail lines, and the
redevelopment of over 1,300 stations (Source: Economic Times). These efforts are being coordinated under the PM Gati
Shakti National Master Plan, which has identified 434 railway projects across key logistics corridors (Source: Press
Information Bureau Research Unit). This increases the EPC opportunities for players across the market. The planned
investments and infrastructure expansion are driving demand for electrification to enable faster, energy-efficient, and
sustainable rail operations across freight corridors, high-speed lines, and redeveloped stations.

A few instances can be seen through the targeted capital allocations for FY26 as outlined below:

Increasing Private Participation through Schemes likes Station Re -development is unlocking EPC Growth


                                                                         159
Amrit Bharat Station Scheme (ABSS) is transforming over 1,300 stations with modern facilities, cultural integration, and
urban connectivity improvements. While initially positioned as a PPP-driven initiative, limited private interest shifted the
execution model towards EPC contracts, creating a pipeline of nearly INR 30,000 crore worth of opportunities for EPC
players over the next two years (Source: ICRA). A select set of stations, including Rani Kamlapati, Pune, and Chennai
Central, are being developed under the PPP model, but the bulk of the scheme relies on EPC, ensuring steady private
participation through contracts while keeping investor risk minimal. The infusion of private capital in redevelopment
projects further expands opportunities for EPC players, enabling them to capture value in both execution and
ancillary development.

Urbanization and City Expansion Fueling Rail Infrastructure Demand
India’s urban share is expected to rise from ~30% to 40–50% over the next 20–25 years, with 60+ million-plus cities
contributing ~70% of GDP—a shift that concentrates travel demand and justifies sustained capex in metros, suburban
corridors, and station redevelopment. As large cities densify and Tier-2/3 cities scale up, EPC needs expand across civil
works, OHE, and S&T packages for multimodal hubs and decongestion projects.

India’s Drinking Water and Waste Water Treatment Market

Rapid Increase in Policy driven Investments is Driving Growth of Public Water Infrastructure
Policy-driven investments are accelerating India’s water and wastewater treatment market, boosting demand
for private players. Flagship programs like Jal Jeevan Mission, AMRUT 2.0, and Namami Gange are driving large-
scale projects in piped water supply, STPs, river rejuvenation, and reuse. Urban initiatives such as Delhi’s Yamuna
cleanup, Bengaluru’s INR 3,700 crore lake revival, and Vizag’s INR 1,200 crore desalination plant reflect rising
investment. New CPCB norms and reuse policies are pushing adoption of advanced technologies including tertiary
treatment, decentralized STPs, desalination, and smart water systems. PPP models, green bonds, and multilateral
funding are also expanding private sector participation, driving sustained growth in capital expenditure across the
sector.

Figure 0-25: Key Government Policies impacting Drinking Water and Waste Water Treatment Market




                                               Source: Ministry of Housing & Urban Affairs


Government Policies combat Water Stress require appropriate infrastructure
Globally, water stress varies widely, with many regions in South America, Central Africa, and Northern Europe
experiencing low to moderate levels of pressure on freshwater resources. Developed economies such as the United States,
Canada, and much of Western Europe generally fall in the medium to low stress category, with only a few localised areas
facing high scarcity. By contrast, India falls into the “extremely high” stress bracket, with more than 80% of available
renewable water resources already being withdrawn annually placing it among the most water-stressed nations worldwide
and highlighting a challenge far more acute than that faced by most developed and other major developing countries.
(Note: Low (<10%), Low–medium (10–20%), Medium–high (20–40%), High (40–80%), Extremely high (>80%).)




                                                                 160
India faces acute urban and industrial water stress, with only 28% of urban wastewater currently treated, raising
serious concerns over scarcity and pollution (Source: Centre for Science and Environment). To address this, the
Government of India has launched major initiatives backed by significant investments to expand drinking water
access, build sewage treatment plants, and promote wastewater recycling.

These efforts are creating strong demand for Engineering, Procurement & Construction (EPC) players to design and
execute large-scale infrastructure such as treatment plants, recycling systems, smart water infrastructure, and
pipeline networks. As a result, capital expenditure in water infrastructure is rising, positioning EPC companies at
the core of India’s push for sustainable water management.

Emergence of Advanced Treatment Technologies drive EPC demand

Adoption of advanced treatment technologies membrane bioreactors (MBRs), advanced oxidation processes (AOPs),
electrochemical systems and AI/IoT-enabled digital twins is accelerating as government and industrial actors upgrade
facilities to meet tighter reuse and discharge standards. Further, this is accelerating demand across the Drinking Water
& Wastewater Treatment market for advanced treatment assets and its EPC.

Stringent Environmental & Public Health Regulations

There is a persistent gap between sewage generated and treated across urban centers, driving regulatory urgency for new
and upgraded STPs and ETPs. In response, state agencies and ULBs are accelerating project execution under AMRUT
2.0, which mandates SCADA-based monitoring and advanced automation in approved sewerage works. Simultaneously,
updated OCEMS norms for real-time effluent tracking are pushing industries toward technology-led compliance—
broadening EPC demand across civil, electro-mechanical, and automation packages. (Source: Central Pollution Control
Board)

Aging Infrastructure & Need for Upgrades

Legacy networks and under-capacity plants are being overhauled through mission funding: under AMRUT 2.0, approved
projects already propose 4,814 MLD of new STP capacity, alongside city-level reforms targeting NRW <20%—both of
which require pipeline rehabilitation, DMA creation, pressure management, energy-efficient pumping, and SCADA
integration.

India Transmission and Distribution Market

Rising Power Demand & Industrial Load Growth Driving Network Expansion

India’s electricity demand continues to surge, with peak demand touching 250 GW in FY2024–25 and expected to reach
nearly 270 GW by FY2026, driven by industrial expansion, data centers, and urbanization (Source: Ministry of Power).
This load growth is prompting utilities to expand 400 kV and 765 kV networks, strengthen substations, and develop new
interconnection corridors. States such as Karnataka and Maharashtra are upgrading to higher-voltage systems to support


                                                                161
large industrial parks and technology clusters. Public utilities like POWERGRID and private developers such as Adani
Energy Solutions are scaling up capital expenditure to meet this demand, creating a sustained pipeline for transmission
EPC firms (Source: Adani Energy Solutions).

Technology Shift and Reconductoring Enabling Faster Capacity Addition

Right-of-way constraints and urban congestion are leading utilities to adopt High-Temperature Low-Sag (HTLS)
reconductoring and compact tower technologies to boost corridor capacity without building new lines (Source: CEA).
Reconductoring can effectively double line capacity within shorter project cycles, making it an efficient solution for dense
urban and industrial zones. Indian manufacturers like APAR Industries and Sterlite Power are executing major
reconductoring and uprating projects, offering faster commissioning and minimal downtime. This shift favors EPC firms
equipped for live-line upgrades, bay expansions, and compact tower deployment, adding a specialized niche within
India’s transmission modernization program (Source: IEEMA).

Electric Mobility Expansion Accelerating Urban Distribution Reinforcement

India’s transition to e-mobility is adding new layers of demand to urban power networks. Over 2 million electric vehicles
were sold in FY2024–25, while the number of public charging stations approached 30,000 nationwide (Source: NITI
Aayog). The rollout of the PM E-DRIVE program, providing dedicated funding for public charging infrastructure, is
accelerating the creation of EV corridors across major cities and highways. DISCOMs such as DHBVN and BESCOM
are strengthening 11–33 kV feeders, upgrading distribution transformers, and adopting smart load management systems
to manage evening charging peaks. This transition is generating recurring EPC opportunities in urban feeder
reinforcement, automation, and charging substation deployment (Source: Ministry of Power).

Technological Advancement

With 20.33 crore smart meters sanctioned and 2.41 crore installed as of July 15, 2025, DISCOMs must upgrade

has surged 5X from 2022 to early 2025, growing from 5,151 stations to 29,277, at a ~78.5% CAGR over three years
(Source: Ministry of Heavy Industries). The combined rise of EV adoption and charging infrastructure is increasing load
demand in urban centers, transport depots, and commercial facilities, fueling the need for robust HV and LV
distribution panels to ensure safe and reliable power supply.

Distribution Reforms and Substation Capacity Enhancement
The Revamped Distribution Sector Scheme (RDSS), launched by the Government of India with a total outlay of INR
3.03 lakh crore till FY26, is driving significant investment in distribution infrastructure. A key focus of the scheme is
strengthening and augmenting substation capacity, alongside modernization of distribution networks to reduce AT&C
losses and improve reliability (Source: Ministry of Power). Within this push, technologies such as Compact Substations
(CSS) are gaining traction as utilities look for space-efficient and modular solutions that can be deployed in dense urban
areas and rapidly growing industrial zones. The emphasis on capacity enhancement under RDSS is expected to directly
spur demand for HV and LV panels, as well as allied equipment such as CSS.

India SCADA and Automation Systems Market

Policies are Driving SCADA Integration in India’s Utility and Industrial Sectors

India’s push for SCADA integration is being led by key policies like the Smart Cities Mission, AMRUT 2.0, and
the Revamped Distribution Sector Scheme (RDSS). These initiatives are embedding SCADA into urban infrastructure
to improve reliability, efficiency, and real-time control.

In Smart Cities, SCADA powers Integrated Command and Control Centers (ICCCs) for monitoring utilities like
water, power, and traffic. AMRUT 2.0 mandates SCADA for water network management and leak detection. Further,
RDSS projects like in Noida have earmarked INR 396 crore for SCADA-backed grid automation.

As utilities expand, SCADA systems are becoming vital for deployment in dense urban areas. On the industrial front,
sectors like steel, cement, and chemicals are adopting SCADA for automation, energy efficiency, and predictive
maintenance aligning with India’s digitalization goals.
Together, these efforts are making SCADA central to managing urban utilities and optimizing industrial operations.

Remote / Unmanned Operations Drives Demand
India’s utilities are shifting to remote-controlled and unmanned substations to cut downtime and manpower costs. CEA’s
technical standards and the RDSS scheme promote centralized SCADA/DMS control and automation of field assets, with
grant support up to 90% for such projects. State utilities like Andhra Pradesh and Gujarat have begun converting
substations to fully remote operation, creating sustained EPC demand for control systems, sensors, and secure
communication networks. (Source: Ministry of Power)

IoT and AI as Enablers of SCADA Growth in India
The use of IoT and AI is gradually expanding in SCADA and automation systems across India. These technologies are
being applied to improve monitoring, control, and maintenance in both urban infrastructure and industrial operations.

Companies such as Britannia Industries and Itanta have implemented IoT-based SCADA across production lines.
These systems enable real-time tracking of production metrics and automate functionalities such as receiving of fault
alerts, changing production speeds etc.

While IoT adoption is already widespread, AI integration is still emerging. Companies such as Tata Steel and Bharat
Forge have started using AI for tasks like predictive maintenance and process optimization. As more industries explore
these tools, AI is expected to become a standard part of SCADA systems for improving operational efficiency and
reliability.

Challenges in the Market

Regulatory Landscape

Regulatory Landscape of India’s Railway EPC Market

The landscape for Railway EPC is governed by key listed regulations: -

The Railways Act, 1989



                                                          168
Enacted in 1989 and amended multiple times, this Act provides the legal foundation for railway development, safety, and
land use. It empowers authorities to acquire land, regulate construction, and oversee operations. Compliance requires
executing works strictly as per notified procedures for acquisition, design, and safety, ensuring no deviation from statutory
railway standards.

Railway Board Circulars and Manuals

Issued periodically and updated over time, these circulars and manuals define technical standards, engineering practices,
and SOPs for civil, electrical, and mechanical works. Compliance entails incorporating the latest specifications into
planning, design, and execution to meet operational and safety benchmarks.

Indian Railways General Conditions of Contract (GCC)

Launched as a standard contracting framework and updated regularly, the GCC prescribes obligations, timelines,
penalties, and quality norms for executing works. Alignment involves adhering to contract timelines, quality standards,
and documentation requirements to avoid disputes and penalties.

Indian Railways Works Manual / Unified SSR

Introduced to standardize estimation and execution of works, these documents lay down cost norms and procedural
workflows. Compliance includes using prescribed rates, preparing accurate estimates, and following established
procedures for budgeting, approvals, and execution.

RFCTLARR (Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement)
Act, 2013

It ensures fair compensation, transparency, and rehabilitation for landowners affected by public or private projects. It
mandates social impact assessments, consent from landowners, and compensation, replacing the 1894 Land Acquisition
Act.

Manual for Procurement of Works (MoF)

First issued by the Ministry of Finance in 2019 and updated in 2022, this manual sets rules for tendering, contracting, and
execution of public works. Compliance requires transparent bidding, adherence to timelines, and following prescribed
procurement protocols during all project stages.
These regulations ensure that railway EPC projects follow strict legal, technical, and procedural standards. They make
compliance with land acquisition, safety, contracting, cost norms, and procurement rules an essential part of project
execution.Figure 0-29: Impact of Major Regulatory on Railway EPC Players




                                                    Source: Ken Research Analysis


                                                               169
Regulatory Landscape of India’s Drinking Water and Waste Water Treatment Market

The regulatory landscape for Drinking Water and Waste Water Treatment is governed by the following guidelines and
acts:-

Water (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1974
This act established the legal framework for controlling water pollution through the creation of CPCB and SPCBs,
requiring prior consent for any discharge into water bodies.

Environment (Protection) Act, 1986
A comprehensive law empowering the central government to set environmental standards, including for wastewater
discharge, and enforce them nationwide.

CPCB Guidelines & MOEF&CC Notification (2017)
CPCB proposed STP standards in 2015, which became legally binding after MOEF&CC’s 2017 notification, setting
discharge norms for BOD and TSS based on city classification.

Central Ground Water Authority (CGWA) Guidelines
These guidelines regulate groundwater extraction, requiring industries and municipalities to obtain NOCs and follow
sustainable usage practices.

National Water Policy, 2012
A strategic policy promoting integrated water resource management, prioritizing drinking water needs, and encouraging
reuse of treated wastewater.

Water CESS Act (1977, amended 2003)
Allows authorities to levy charges on water consumption, especially by industries, to fund pollution control and water
conservation efforts.

These regulations mandate effluent treatment, set discharge standards, and restrict groundwater use. The Water and
Environment Acts, CPCB norms, and CGWA guidelines enforce compliance, while the Water CESS Act adds economic
accountability. The National Water Policy further emphasizes reuse, making treatment and recycling essential parts of
water management.

Figure 0-30: Impact of major regulations on Drinking Water and Wastewater EPC players




                                                 Source: Ken Research Analysis




                                                            170
Regulatory Landscape of India’s Transmission and Distribution Market

The regulatory landscape for Transmission and Distribution infrastructure is governed by the following guidelines and
acts:-

Transmission System Planning & Development Regulations, 2021

Establishes coordinated national and state-level grid planning linked to 500+ GW renewable targets. Ensures transparent
tariff recovery and promotes competitive bidding (TBCB), boosting private EPC participation.

Rights of Way (RoW) Rules, 2016 (Amended 2023)

Standardizes compensation and clearance processes for overhead and underground lines. Reduces project delays and eases
execution for transmission contractors.

Central Transmission Utility (CTU) & State Transmission Utility (STU) Regulations, 2020

Define responsibilities for grid planning, approvals, and inter-state coordination, improving efficiency in project rollout.

Electric Vehicle Charging Infrastructure Guidelines, 2022

Set technical and tariff standards for EV charging networks. Trigger distribution-level reinforcement and new connection
demand.

General Network Access (GNA) Regulations, 2022

Redefines access to the national grid, allowing flexible and efficient capacity use for renewable and storage projects.
Enhances transmission utilization and expands EPC opportunities in inter- and intra-state corridors.

Regulatory Landscape of India’s HT / LT Distribution Panels & Compact Sub-Stations Market

The landscape for HT/LT distribution panels and compact substations is anchored by:




                                                               171
Electricity Act, 2003

Parent law governing generation, transmission, distribution, and electrical safety across India. Provides statutory
backing for compliance and empowers regulatory authorities.

CEA (Measures Relating to Safety and Electric Supply) Regulations, 2023

Prescribes mandatory safety norms for design, installation, operation, and maintenance of electrical systems to
prevent hazards and ensure reliable supply.

CEA Technical Standards for Construction of Electrical Plants & Lines, 2022

Defines technical requirements for construction and integration of substations, plants, and lines, ensuring
uniformity and safe grid connectivity.

BIS Standards (IS 8623:1993, IS 14786:2000)

Indian Standards that set design and performance requirements for LT panels (IS 8623) and prefabricated substations (IS
14786).

CPRI Type Test Certification

Independent testing of panels and substations by CPRI/NABL labs to validate busbar ratings, thermal withstand, and
safety performance.

Regulatory Landscape Of India’s Scada And Automation Systems Market

The regulatory landscape for SCADA and Automation Systems is governed by the following guidelines and acts:-

Electricity Act, 2003
It is the legal backbone for power sector operations, grid standards, and system reliability. It mandates monitoring,
scheduling, and dispatch systems — SCADA/DMS becomes a tool to comply.

CEA Safety & Grid Standards Regulations (2010, 2022)
Ensure reliable grid operations, data availability, and stability. It demands for real-time monitoring and data acquisition
to maintain grid discipline.

CERC Communication System Regulations (2017)
Mandates communication infrastructure for real-time monitoring. SCADA systems must seamlessly integrate with Wide
Area Measurement Systems (WAMS) and PMUs.



                                                              172
National Smart Grid Mission (NSGM), 2015
Modernize the grid through smart automation, demand management, and advanced metering and SCADA is at the core
of smart grid rollouts.

MoP Cybersecurity Guidelines (2017/2021)
It establish enforceable baseline rules for all power-sector entities (utilities, vendors, OEMs) to systematize cyber
governance, IT/OT segregation, logging and monitoring, incident response, audits, and secure procurement.

IS/IEC standards (15953, 61850, 62351, etc.)
It comprises of communication protocols for substation automation, cybersecurity for power system control and SCADA.
These regulations are essential for ensuring grid reliability, real-time monitoring, secure communication, and compliance
with evolving smart grid standards in India.

Government Initiatives

Government-led infrastructure programs are reshaping India’s core sectors, creating sustained opportunities for EPC
players. In particular, flagship initiatives in railways and drinking water & wastewater management are driving large-
scale demand for engineering, construction, and systems integration.

Initiatives Driving Demand for Railway EPC Players

Major Government Initiatives Creating Demand for EPC Player are:-

•        Vande Bharat Scheme

         Flagship semi–high-speed train program targeting pan-India deployment of new-generation trainsets. It aims
         Manufacture and operates 200 Vande Bharat trains within three years, supported by dedicated maintenance
         depots, upgraded stations, and modern signaling. This drives large civil, mechanical, and electrical EPC contracts
         ~INR 30,000–40,000 crore for depots, electrification, and signaling system upgrades.

•        Rail Land Development Authority (RLDA) Projects

         RLDA oversees commercial redevelopment of railway land, stations, and colonies.It aims at redevelop ~15 major
         colonies and stations into self-sustaining complexes while monetizing assets worth ~INR 2.25 lakh crore.This
         generates long-term EPC and PPP opportunities in civil works, utilities, and electrical infrastructure, including
         EPC-cum-O&M models.

•        Regional Rapid Transit System (RRTS)

                                                              173
       First-of-its-kind regional high-speed transit network under NCRTC. It aims at Implement Delhi–Meerut, Delhi–
       Alwar, and Delhi–Panipat corridors using Namo Bharat trains (up to 180 km/h) to reduce travel time and
       congestion. Expands EPC scope in viaduct construction, signaling, 25 kV AC electrification, and multimodal
       station integration, setting a precedent for Tier-1 and Tier-2 networks.

•      Dedicated Freight Corridors (DFC)

       Backbone freight network under the PM Gati Shakti Plan. It aims at complete Western and Eastern DFCs and
       extend to East–West, North–South, and East–Coast Corridors, with FY26 capex of ~₹500 crore. This boosts
       demand for track works, signaling, power systems, and logistics hubs, improving freight capacity and operational
       efficiency.

•      Speed Improvement Program (SIP)

       Network-wide modernization initiative for faster passenger train movement. It aims at upgrading 30,000 km of
       existing lines for 120–160 km/h operations through track renewal, bridge strengthening, automatic signaling
       (Kavach), and OHE enhancements. It spurs EPC opportunities in civil, signaling, and traction power
       modernization, with integrated upgrades across major corridors.

•      Freight Tonnage Expansion Plan

       Strategic initiative to scale India’s rail freight capacity in line with industrial and logistics growth. It aims at
       increasing freight volume from 1.6 Bn tonnes (FY24) to 3 Bn tonnes by 2030, using ~3,000 MT-capacity rakes,
       heavier axle loads, and new goods terminals, GCTs, and multimodal parks. It creates sustained EPC and MEP
       demand across terminal construction, logistics hubs, traction systems, and yard modernization, integrating with
       DFCs, ports, and industrial corridors.

Figure 0-34:Major Government Initiatives creating demand for EPC Players




                                                  Source: Ken Research Analysis


•      Mission Electrification

       A national initiative by Indian Railways to achieve 100% electrification of broad-gauge routes, enhancing energy
       efficiency and reducing fuel dependence. Between FY2018 and FY2023, over 58,000 route kilometers were
       electrified, establishing India as one of the world’s largest electrified rail networks. The program drove strong
       EPC demand in OHE works, traction substations, power distribution, and SCADA integration, modernizing rail
       infrastructure across key corridors.



                                                             174
•        Station Redevelopment

         A flagship program to redevelop 1,300+ railway stations into modern, passenger-centric, and multi-modal hubs.
         Aims to enhance commuter experience through upgraded concourses, platforms, circulation areas, and urban
         integration, implemented under PPP and EPC-cum-O&M frameworks. This creates significant EPC
         opportunities in civil construction, architectural design, MEP systems, and electrical and signaling integration,
         transforming railway stations into integrated transport and commercial centers.

•        DDMC & High-Speed Rapid Railways:

         Opportunities for EPC players lie in developing regional and high-speed corridors enhancing urban–rural
         connectivity. These projects drive demand for civil works, track laying, electrification, and signaling. As India
         expands intercity and semi-high-speed routes, EPC scope grows across design, construction, and integrated
         system works.

Impact of Regional Tendering on Market Accessibility and Execution

The shift to regional tendering in railway EPC has redefined how projects are awarded and executed. By empowering
zonal authorities to issue tenders, the system has opened doors for firms with strong local presence and operational agility.
This decentralization has led to a more competitive environment, where participation is no longer limited to large national
players.

A key outcome of this model is the acceleration of project timelines. Zonal fast-track mechanisms have reduced tender
processing durations from 2–3 years to just 6–9 months. This has enabled quicker mobilization, faster ground execution,
and improved alignment with regional infrastructure priorities.

As a result, execution capabilities have strengthened, and the overall efficiency of the railway infrastructure ecosystem
has improved.

Initiatives Driving Demand for EPC Players under Drinking water and Waste Water Treatment Market

India’s efforts to strengthen water security are creating new work for engineering, procurement, and construction
companies through three major government programs. The Jal Jeevan Mission, extended to 2028, is modernizing
treatment plants, using advanced technologies, and ensuring long-term operations in rural areas. The Atal Mission for
Rejuvenation and Urban Transformation 2.0 is expanding urban water and sewage networks across 500 cities with a
focus on innovation and efficiency. The Namami Gange Mission, with an investment of thirty thousand crore rupees, is
rejuvenating the Ganga River basin through advanced treatment plants and green financing. Together, these programs
combine scale, technology, and sustainability, placing engineering, procurement, and construction firms at the
front of India’s water infrastructure growth.

AMRUT & AMRUT 2.0

Launched in 2015 and expanded in 2021, AMRUT and AMRUT 2.0 aim to transform urban water infrastructure across
500+ cities. The combined missions focus on universal coverage of tap and sewer connections, rejuvenation of water
bodies, and smart monitoring through SCADA systems. With a total budget of INR 2.99 lakh crore, they have already
delivered over 2 crore tap and 1.5 crore sewer connections, while also enhancing the capacity of Urban Local Bodies
(Source: India Water Portal). These initiatives are unlocking large-scale EPC opportunities in water supply, treatment,
and urban resilience, making them central to India’s urban infrastructure strategy.

National Green Tribunal (NGT)
NGT has introduced a regulatory push through its enforcement of Zero Liquid Discharge (ZLD) norms across key
industrial sectors such as textiles, chemicals, pharmaceuticals, and tanneries. Over 2,000 industrial units have been
identified for compliance upgrades, creating a robust pipeline of EPC work in industrial clusters across Tamil Nadu,
Gujarat, and Maharashtra. EPC firms with expertise in process engineering and industrial automation are particularly
well-suited to deliver retrofitting solutions involving technologies like reverse osmosis (RO), multiple-effect evaporators
(MEE), and agitated thin film dryers (ATFD). There is also growing interest in bundling operations and maintenance
(O&M) contracts to ensure long-term sustainability and revenue continuity.

                   Figure 0-35: NGT Enforcement Driving Industrial Water EPC Opportunities




                                                            175
                                                   Source: Ken Research Analysis


Together, these initiatives represent a tailwind for India’s Water EPC sector. With combined funding and a clear policy
thrust toward sustainability, compliance, and infrastructure modernization, EPC firms that can deliver integrated, tech-
enabled, and scalable solutions.

Jal Jeevan Mission

Jal Jeevan Mission (launched in 2019) is generating large-scale demand for water treatment plants, distribution
pipelines, and monitoring solutions. The Union Budget FY25–26, the government increased the Mission’s outlay to INR
67,000 crore and extended it to 2028, targeting 100% coverage within three years (Source: Ministry of Finance). By
targeting every rural household with functional tap water, the mission has expanded the market footprint into remote
geographies and created steady opportunities for EPC players specializing in low-cost and sustainable water supply
systems.

River Restoration Plans

National Mission for clean Ganga is an initiative under the Namami Gange mission, launched in 2014 with the aim of
rejuvenating and conserving the Ganga River, with a estimated budget allocation of INR 3,400 crore in FY25-FY26
(Source: Ministry of Jal Shakti). It is an integrated conservation mission launched by the Government of India to
rejuvenate the Ganga River through initiatives like sewerage treatment, river-front development, and biodiversity
enhancement. Key components of the mission include river-surface cleaning, afforestation, public awareness, industrial
effluent monitoring, and the development of Ganga Gram. As this mission, aims to improve water quality and enhance
the ecosystem, plans such as the sewage treatment development and the industrial effluent monitoring are expected
to increase the EPC opportunities in the market.

The Yamuna Action Plan and river restoration projects for rivers such as the Musi, Cooum, and Sabarmati focus on
reducing pollution, afforestation, and riverfront development. These measures directly intersect with the water and water
treatment sector, as reducing untreated sewage and industrial effluents entering rivers requires extensive deployment of
sewage treatment plants, effluent treatment plants, and decentralized treatment systems (Source: Namami Gange
Programme).

Smart Cities Mission

The Smart Cities Mission, with an outlay of INR 1.64 lakh crore and nearly 93% project completion, has been a
major growth driver for India’s drinking water and wastewater treatment market. (Source: Smart Cities Mission)
Many projects focus on water supply, smart metering, SCADA-based leakage detection, and sewerage upgrades,
driving sustained EPC demand. By integrating automation and digital monitoring, the mission has shifted the
market toward tech-enabled solutions. As utilities emphasize real-time water quality, analytics, and efficient
sewage management, EPC opportunities are created in advanced STPs, IoT-based monitoring, and
decentralized treatment systems.

Initiatives Driving Demand for Transmission and Distribution in India


                                                              176
India’s efforts to strengthen its electricity grid and integrate renewable energy are generating consistent opportunities for
engineering, procurement, and construction (EPC) companies. Three major government programs define the current
policy landscape:

Revamped Distribution Sector Scheme (RDSS):

Launched in 2021 with an investment of over ₹3 trillion, RDSS aims to modernize India’s power distribution
network through feeder segregation, system strengthening, and smart meter deployment. It links funding to loss
reduction and billing efficiency, ensuring continuous EPC demand across substation upgrades and digital
infrastructure.

Green Energy Corridor (GEC):

Implemented in two phases, the GEC is building high-voltage transmission corridors to evacuate renewable power
from generation zones to demand centers. Covering over 10,000 ckm of intra -state and inter-state lines, it has
created strong EPC demand in Rajasthan, Gujarat, and Tamil Nadu.

National Electricity Plan (NEP) 2023–2032:

The NEP outlines the addition of 1.9 lakh circuit kilometers of new transmission lines and major substation capacity
expansion to enable 500 GW of renewable integration by 2030. It promotes private participation through tariff -
based competitive bidding, widening EPC opportunities at both central and state levels.

Together, these initiatives combine grid modernization, renewable integration, and digital transformation ,
providing a long-term, policy-backed pipeline for India’s transmission and distribution EPC sector.

Initiatives Driving Demand for Power Distribution Panels and CSS Market in India

Government programs such as the Revamped Distribution Sector Scheme (RDSS) and the Green Energy Corridor
(GEC)—outlined under India’s Transmission and Distribution market—also underpin demand for power distribution
panels and compact substations by strengthening grid reliability and renewable integration.
Beyond these, urban development initiatives have emerged as major growth drivers for electrical and automation
systems. The Smart Cities Mission, AMRUT 2.0, and Make in India programs are modernizing urban infrastructure,
driving large-scale deployment of LT/HT panels, compact substations, and intelligent control systems across
commercial, industrial, and residential projects.

These schemes emphasize energy efficiency, digital monitoring, and space optimization, creating sustained demand
for modular, automation-ready electrical panels and compact substations. As cities expand and industries digitalize,
panel integrators and EPC firms are increasingly central to delivering reliable, safe, and technology-driven urban power
systems.

Initiatives Driving Demand for SCADA and Automation India

SCADA and automation systems serve as a common technological layer across all the infrastructure markets discussed
above. They are integral to railway electrification and signaling, water and wastewater treatment, power
transmission and distribution, and urban electrical networks. As India’s infrastructure shifts toward digital, efficient,
and remotely managed operations, automation is no longer a standalone segment but a core enabler embedded within
EPC and O&M scopes across sectors. This is enhancing reliability, safety, and lifecycle performance.

Competition Landscape

Ecosystem of India’s Railway EPC Market

The Indian Railway Infrastructure Spend is overseen by the Ministry of Railways (MoR) and the Railway Boards of States
and Regions where the work needs to be carried out. Large-scale works are assigned to PSUs like IRCON, RITES, and
RVNL, which act as nodal agencies for project preparation, tendering (via GeM, CPPP, PSU portals), quality supervision,
and sometimes direct EPC execution.

The market is highly competitive, with an estimated 200+ EPC players primarily Indian firms, alongside select global
participants like Siemens, Alstom, and Hitachi in signalling and electrification.


                                                            177
EPC contractors are broadly split into two categories:

•    Fully integrated EPC players: deliver end-to-end projects across track laying, electrification, bridges, signaling,
     and station upgrades, either independently or with PSUs.
•    Domain-specific contractors: specialize in specific verticals such as track laying, electrification, or signalling and
     telecommunication. These firms focus on PSU or integrated EPC tenders, often with higher efficiency in their
     niche.

Players are further classified by annual revenue sizing bands. This indicates the project tender value that the players can
achieve in the Railway EPC market.

Ecosystem of India’s Drinking Water and Wastewater Treatment Market

In the Indian drinking water and wastewater infrastructure sector large EPC contracts are tendered through state
procurement portals and in cases of industrial plants EPC contracts are often negotiated. And localized packages of the
large EPC contracts are often bid to regional specialists.

On basis of this, the ecosystem of players in India’s drinking water and wastewater market can broadly be classified into
three categories:

•   Turnkey EPC Solution Providers: These companies deliver the full scope of work from design and engineering to
    procurement, installation, and commissioning of treatment plants.
•   Technology Providers: These companies provide proprietary treatment equipment, modules, and technologies that
    are integrated into projects by EPC contractors.
•   Focused EPC & Service Providers: These are smaller players that execute specific packages within larger projects,
    such as civil works, electrical panels, SCADA & automation, or modular STPs/ETPs.

Ecosystem of India’s Transmission and Distribution Market

The Indian Transmission and Distribution (T&D) market covers extra-high-voltage transmission systems and medium- to
low-voltage distribution networks. Projects are implemented under central and state programs such as RDSS, Green
Energy Corridor, and Tariff-Based Competitive Bidding (TBCB). The market is moderately fragmented, with about
250–300 active players across transmission, distribution, and equipment supply. Execution responsibility is divided
between public sector undertakings, large EPC firms, and regional contractors. Ecosystem participants can be grouped
into two categories:

•   Turnkey EPC Players: Execute complete projects involving design, procurement, installation, and commissioning.
    These firms typically handle 132–765 kV lines, substations, and renewable evacuation systems.
•   Subcontracting and Regional Execution Players: Operate mainly in 11–220 kV sub-transmission and distribution
    works under state DISCOMs and RDSS programs. They execute feeder segregation, substation upgrades, cabling,
    and metering projects, often as subcontractors to larger EPCs.

Ecosystem of India’s Power Distribution Panels and Compact Substation Market

The Indian power distribution panel and compact substation market serves industrial, commercial, and utility customers.
There are players who assemble complete panels and compact substations, delivering ready-to-install solutions. Others
manufacture specific components such as breakers, switches, relays, and busbars that are integrated into these
assemblies.

On this basis, the ecosystem of players in India’s market can broadly be classified into two categories:

•   Complete Assembly Providers: These companies deliver fully assembled HT/LT panels or compact substations.
•   Component Suppliers: These companies manufacture and supply individual electrical components that are
    integrated into assemblies.

Ecosystem of India’s SCADA and Automation Market

The Indian SCADA and automation market spans across power, water, oil & gas, transport, and industrial applications.
Large-scale projects are typically embedded within EPC contracts or smart city/state utility programs, with execution led



                                                           178
by a mix of multinational firms and regional specialists. The market is estimated to have 120–150 active players, ranging
from global automation leaders to localized integrators.

Ecosystem participants can be broadly split into two categories:

•     Turnkey SCADA & Automation Integrators: Deliver end-to-end solutions covering design, integration, installation,
      and commissioning of automation systems.
•     Technology & Platform Providers: Supply proprietary SCADA software, PLCs, RTUs, sensors, and industrial IoT
      platforms that are integrated into projects by system integrators

Overview of Major Players in India’s Infrastructure EPC Market

This section includes a cross-comparison between peers operating in India’s Infrastructure EPC Market.

Company Profiles:

Core4 Engineers Limited: Incorporated on 2022, the company operates as an electrical-infrastructure and EPC-focused
company. The company derives majority of its revenue from water and wastewater treatment, and railway EPC works. It
also operates in the transmission and panel segment. The product and solution portfolio spans HT panels, LT distribution
boards, power & control centers motor control centers (MCC), compact substations, and SCADA-linked electrical
solutions, serving utility and infrastructure project requirements.

Trimurthi HITECH Co. Pvt. Ltd: Incorporated in 1989, the company operates as an electrification contractor with
execution exposure concentrated in Indian Railways. Its revenue model is primarily project-based contracting for railway
electrification packages and allied electrical works. The operating portfolio includes overhead electrification and
commissioning of substations/switching stations, cabling, and allied electrification works, with project experience
referenced for Southern Railway.

SN Enviro-Tech Pvt. Ltd: The company is an EPC service provider in water and wastewater infrastructure space. Its
revenue model is anchored in engineering, procurement and construction contracts for public/industrial water systems,
including sewage and effluent treatment projects. The portfolio includes EPC delivery of water & sewage treatment plants
and industrial effluent treatment plants, alongside associated civil and systems execution as part of turnkey project scopes.

K2 Infragen Ltd: Incorporated in 2015, it operates as an integrated EPC and core infrastructure player with multi-state
execution exposure. Its revenue model is diversified across EPC contract revenues, services/project structuring &
execution support, and (as disclosed in offer-note summaries) trading/procurement-led revenues alongside core EPC. The
portfolio covers end-to-end execution (design to commissioning) across water supply projects, railway projects, road
projects, civil construction works, and related infrastructure builds, with delivery spanning multiple Indian states.

Overview




We are an Engineering, Procurement, Construction and Commissioning (“EPCC”) company engaged in providing
integrated infrastructure solutions across multiple domains, with a primary focus on the railway infrastructure, power
transmission & distribution, and water & wastewater treatment sectors. Our expertise spans the entire project lifecycle
design, engineering, procurement, erection, testing, commissioning, and operation & maintenance (“O&M”). We also
operate an in-house manufacturing facility for High-Tension (“HT”) and Low-Tension (“LT”) electrical panels and
compact substations, enabling us to offer customized, reliable, and cost-efficient products that complement our EPCC
activities. We also undertake sub-contracting assignments, providing on-ground execution support for a wide range of
engineering projects.




                                                             182
India’s EPC industry delivers services including design and engineering, procurement, civil works, installation,
commissioning and operation and maintenance covering Railway EPC, Drinking Water & Wastewater Treatment, Power
Distribution Panels and Compact Substation, Transmission and Distribution and SCADA and Automation. India’s
Railway EPC market grew from INR 16.2 thousand crore in FY 20 to INR 30.4 thousand crore in FY 25 and is expected
to reach INR 50.5 thousand crore by FY 30F. The drinking water and wastewater market is projected to reach INR 169.6
thousand crore by FY 30F, supported by growth across panels, transmission and distribution and SCADA segments.
Indian Infrastructure EPC Market is defined as the total domestic revenue generated from engineering, procurement, and
construction (EPC) activities undertaken within India across Railway Infrastructure and Water Infrastructure segments,
along with the related markets for HT/LT Power Distribution Panels, Compact Substations (CSS), and SCADA &
Automation Systems. (Source: Ken Report)

We operate through five interlinked business segments, each contributing to our integrated infrastructure and engineering
solutions framework. Incorporated with the vision of delivering technically robust and cost-effective engineering
solutions, we offer end-to-end project execution capabilities covering design, engineering, procurement, project
management, construction, installation, testing and commissioning.

Our diversified business verticals include:

(a) Railway Electrification & Infrastructure:

Railway Electrification (RE) – We undertake RE and allied infrastructure works represent one of our principal business
segments. We undertake EPCC projects involving the design, supply, erection, testing and commissioning of 25 kV AC
Overhead Electrification (“OHE”) systems, Traction Sub-stations (“TSS”), and Sectioning and Paralleling Posts
(“SP/SSP”). Our scope also includes associated civil works such as foundations, trenches, control room buildings, and
ancillary structures, as well as signalling and telecommunication interface works. We execute projects for zonal railways,
public sector undertakings, and large infrastructure contractors. The Company’s technical proficiency and adherence to
RDSO standards enable efficient, safe, and reliable electrification execution.

Railway Infrastructure Works – Our company does composite nature of work involving civil, electrical, and mechanical
works as part of the Railway Station Redevelopment with allied works and modernization programs initiated by Indian
Railways under the “Amrit Bharat Station Scheme” and other national initiatives. Our services in this domain cover
structural rehabilitation, construction of passenger amenities, illumination systems, internal and external electrification,
foot over bridges, water supply and drainage systems, digital LED signages and integration of automation for energy
management. Through these works, we contribute to the modernization of passenger interface infrastructure and
enhancement of service standards across the Indian Railways network.

Indian Infrastructure EPC Market is defined as the total domestic revenue generated from engineering, procurement, and
construction (EPC) activities undertaken within India across Railway Infrastructure and Water Infrastructure segments,
along with the related markets for HT/LT Power Distribution Panels, Compact Substations (CSS), and SCADA &
Automation Systems. (Source: Ken Report)

The Railway EPC Market is defined as the domestic revenue generated from EPC contracting activities related to railway
electrification, signaling & telecommunication, and civil works in India. Between FY 20 and FY 25, the Railway EPC
market increased from INR 16.2 thousand crore to INR 30.4 thousand crore, at a CAGR of 13.4%. From FY 25 to FY
30F, the market is expected to grow to INR 50.5 thousand crore, at a CAGR of 10.7%. (Source: Ken Report)

In FY 25, India’s Railway EPC market on segmentation by work type, composite infrastructure works, accounted for
51.0%, followed by Electrification of Railway Lines at 13.8%, S&T Works at 12.8%, PEB for Sheds, Warehouses &
Depots at 9.9%, OHE at 5.6%, Traction Substations at 4.3% and Power Transmission & Distribution Networks at 2.6%.
Opportunities for EPC players lie in the execution of electrification, signaling, and station redevelopment works under
flagship programs such as PM Gati Shakti, Amrit Bharat Station Scheme, and Mission Electrification. In addition, high-
speed rail corridors, dedicated freight lines, and multimodal logistics hubs are creating sustained EPC demand across civil
and electrical packages. (Source: Ken Report)

The India Metro Systems EPC Market is defined as the domestic revenue generated from EPC contracting activities
related exclusively to urban metro rail systems in India. India’s metro EPC market has grown steadily from ₹15,000 crore
in FY 19 to an estimated ₹23,500 crore in FY 25, reflecting a CAGR of 7.8%, and is projected to reach ₹34,700 crore by
FY 30F, reflecting an 8.1% CAGR (FY 25 – FY 30F). (Source: Ken Report)

(b) Extra High Tension (“EHT”) Transmission and Distribution Systems:



                                                            183
Our company undertakes turnkey projects in Extra High Tension Transmission and Distribution Systems, covering voltage
levels up to 220 kV. Its scope includes sub-station construction, installation of power transformers, switchgear, control
and relay panels, busbar systems, and distribution networks. We also execute transmission line projects, including
foundation works, tower erection, conductor stringing, and OPGW (“Optical Ground Wire”) integration. Our work in
this vertical supports utilities, public sector undertakings, and industrial clients in strengthening grid reliability and power
distribution efficiency. Its participation aligns with national programs such as the “Revamped Distribution Sector Scheme
(RDSS) and Green Energy Corridors”, emphasizing grid modernization and renewable integration.

The Transmission and Distribution (T&D) Market is defined as the domestic EPC revenue generated from the design,
supply, construction, and commissioning of transmission lines, substations, and distribution networks across India. As of
FY 25, India’s transmission and distribution market size stood at INR 36,000.0 crore, growing at a strong CAGR of 16.2
% over FY 20 – FY 25. The market is projected to reach INR 60,063.0 crore by FY 30F, at a CAGR of 10.8 % (FY 25 –
FY 30F). (Source: Ken Report)

In FY 25, India’s Transmission and Distribution Market Segmentation (INR ‘000 crore) by End User, state segment
accounted for 66.1%, followed by Central segment at 21.9% and Private segment at 11.9%.Opportunities for EPC players
lie in grid expansion, substation construction, feeder modernization driven by government programs such as the Revamped
Distribution Sector Scheme (RDSS), Green Energy Corridor, and National Electricity Plan, large-scale push for renewable
evacuation and interregional transmission corridors and growing need for reliable power transmission to support water,
industrial, and renewable infrastructure. (Source: Ken Report)

(c) Water and Wastewater Treatment EPCC:

We provide turnkey EPCC solutions for Water Treatment Plants (“WTP”), Sewage Treatment Plants (“STP”), and
Effluent Treatment Plants (“ETP”), along with associated civil, mechanical, and electrical works. Its capabilities cover
intake wells, pumping stations, rising mains, pipelines, and process automation systems. With ensuring compliance with
CPCB and SPCB norms, we execute projects based on STP technologies such as:

•   MBBR (Moving Bed Biofilm Reactor)
•   SBR (Sequencing Batch Reactor)

These works align with government programs like “Jal Jeevan Mission”, “AMRUT”, and “Namami Gange”, supporting
national goals of water conservation, reuse, and sustainable urban development.

The Drinking Water and Waste Water Treatment Market is defined as the domestic EPC revenue generated from the
design, supply, and execution of drinking water treatment plants, wastewater/sewage treatment plants, distribution
networks, pumping stations, and electro-mechanical works in India. India’s drinking water and wastewater treatment
market expanded from INR 60.5 thousand crore in FY 20 to INR 99.9 thousand crore in FY 25, at a CAGR of 10.6%. It
is expected to reach INR 169.6 thousand crore by FY 30F at a CAGR of ~11.2% (FY 25 – FY 30F). (Source: Ken Report)

In FY 25, India’s Drinking Water and Waste Water Treatment on segmentation by plant type, sewage and water piping
accounted for 33.0%, followed by drinking water treatment plants at 28.0%, effluent treatment plants at 18.5%, sewage
treatment plants at 15.5% and associated infrastructure (including pump houses, reservoirs, pipelines, and control rooms)
at 5.0%.(Source: Ken Report)

Opportunities for EPC players lie in the design and execution of drinking water, sewage, and effluent treatment plants
under flagship government programs such as Jal Jeevan Mission, AMRUT 2.0, and Namami Gange. Rising urbanization,
industrial compliance norms, and Zero Liquid Discharge (ZLD) requirements are accelerating investments in STPs, ETPs,
and reuse systems. (Source: Ken Report)

(d) Automation and SCADA Systems:

Automation and Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition (“SCADA”) solutions form an integral part of our service
offerings. We design and implement Programmable Logic Controller (PLC)-based automation systems, RTU and HMI
integration, instrumentation, control panels, and communication networks for remote monitoring and control of
infrastructure assets. Our automation services are applied across its core business sectors railway electrification, water
systems, and power distribution enhancing system reliability, efficiency, and operational safety.

The SCADA & Automation Systems Market is defined as the domestic revenue generated from the design, supply,
execution, and commissioning of SCADA and automation systems across electrical networks, water and wastewater
infrastructure, power projects, and railway installations in India. The Indian SCADA and Automation Systems market has


                                                              184
grown from INR 5.1 thousand crore in FY 20 to INR 7.7 thousand crore in FY 25, reflecting a CAGR of 8.6%. The market
projected to reach INR 12.0 thousand crore by FY 30F, registering a CAGR of 9.3% between FY 25 – FY 30F. (Source:
Ken Report)

In FY 25, India’s SCADA and Automation Systems Market Segmentation by Application, Power Distribution SCADA
accounted for 24.7%, followed by Oil & Gas SCADA at 23.4%, Other Applications SCADA at 16.9%, Manufacturing
SCADA at 15.6%, Water Supply SCADA at 10.4% and Waste Water SCADA at 9.1%. (Source: Ken Report)

The market offers growing opportunities for EPC players in deployment and integration of SCADA systems across power,
water, and industrial assets. With utilities adopting IoT, cloud, and AI-based analytics, EPCs with automation capabilities
can capture value in grid modernization, renewable integration, and smart water networks, supported by government-led
digitalization programs driving steady automation-linked EPC demand. (Source: Ken Report)

(e) Composite supply of HT/LT Distribution Panels along with related services:

We manufacture a wide range of High Tension (HT) and Low Tension (LT) distribution and control panels, including
VCB panels, PCC, MCC, APFC, synchronization panels, and PLC-based automation panels. All panels are designed and
fabricated in accordance with IS/IEC standards, ensuring safety, reliability, and consistent performance. Our in-house
capability supports complete vertical integration from design and fabrication to assembly and testing allowing us to
maintain strict quality control, optimize costs, and ensure timely delivery. In addition to meeting internal project
requirements, this division also contributes to external revenue by supplying panels to third-party clients across industrial
and infrastructure sectors. These panels are typically provided as a composite supply along with our installation, testing
and commissioning services as part of our integrated project execution.

A major strength of this division is our capability to produce Compact Substations (CSS) with capacities up to 2.5 MVA
and voltage levels up to 11 kV. These factory-built, fully integrated substations combine a transformer, HT panel, LT
panel, and protection systems within a single compact enclosure. Their modular design, enhanced safety features, and
reduced installation footprint make them ideal for industrial, commercial, and utility applications. This product segment
represents a key differentiator for us, offering clients faster deployment, improved reliability, and lower lifecycle costs.

The Transmission and Distribution (T&D) Market is defined as the domestic EPC revenue generated from the design,
supply, construction, and commissioning of transmission lines, substations, and distribution networks across India. As of
FY 25, India’s transmission and distribution market size stood at INR 36,000.0 crore, growing at a strong CAGR of 16.2
% over FY 20 – FY 25. The market is projected to reach INR 60,063.0 crore by FY 30F, at a CAGR of 10.8 % (FY 25 –
FY 30F). (Source: Ken Report)

industrial, and renewable infrastructure. (Source: Ken Report)

We began our operations as a partnership firm in 2014 and were converted into a private limited company in 2022 under
the provisions of the Companies Act, 2013. Headquartered in Mysore, Karnataka, we started as an EPC contractor and
gradually expanded into a diversified infrastructure and utility solutions provider with integrated capabilities across
design, engineering, installation, testing, commissioning, and O&M. Over the years, we have built relationships with
government organizations, PSUs, utilities, and private enterprises across India. Our structure allows us to leverage
synergies between our EPC and manufacturing divisions, enabling us to deliver end-to-end, technology-driven, and cost-
optimized infrastructure solutions across sectors.

Our strength lies in integrated engineering capability, experienced technical team, and proven execution across complex,
time-bound projects. Our business model focuses on project management, vendor partnerships, in-house design expertise,
and commitment to quality, safety, and sustainability. We have long-term relationships with public sector undertakings,
state utilities, and private clients, including participation in infrastructure programs led by Indian Railways and other
government agencies. With a presence across multiple sectors and a growing order book, we combine EPC experience
with in-house manufacturing through a vertically integrated model that supports cost efficiency, design flexibility, and
quality control. This enables execution of multidisciplinary projects in power, water, and industrial automation within
defined timelines. Our vision is to enhance execution and profitability in small and medium EPC contracts while adopting
emerging technologies to deliver sustainable infrastructure under Public-Private Partnership (“PPP”) models.

        receivables and closing trade receivables.

        expenses plus changes in Inventories of Work-in-Progress. Average trade payables is calculated as average of opening trade payables and closing trade payables.
(12)    Working capital cycle (days) is calculated inventory days plus trade receivables days minus trade payables days.

Our Revenue Mix

Our revenue is primarily derived from two key segments:

1.      Service Revenue: Generated from Engineering, Procurement, Construction, and Commissioning (EPCC) works
        across Railway Electrification, EHT Transmission & Distribution, and Water & Wastewater Infrastructure projects.
        And SCADA and automation system integration and composite supply of HT/LT Distribution Panels along with
        related services

        supply of High and Low Tension (HT/LT) electrical distribution panels, control and relay panels, PLC and SCADA
        panels, and other custom-built electrical manufacturing. These vertical supports both internal EPC requirements and
        third-party industrial and infrastructure clients.

Our Strengths

We believe that the following competitive strengths have contributed to our business growth and will continue to drive
our success:

a)      Wide operational reach and multi-disciplinary execution capability

We benefit from a broad operational footprint and a diverse multi-disciplinary execution capability that positions it as a
comprehensive engineering solutions provider across critical infrastructure sectors. We operate across a wide range of
specialised service verticals, including Railway Electrification and Infrastructure, EHV Transmission and Distribution
EPCC, Water and Wastewater EPCC, SCADA and Automation, and the in-house manufacturing of HT/LT distribution
panels. This diversified vertical presence enables us to undertake complex, large-scale engineering assignments requiring
integrated solutions across electrical, civil, mechanical, and automation domains.

We have an experience in railway electrification and infrastructure development, including 25 kV Overhead
Electrification (OHE), Traction Substations (TSS), power supply systems, general electrification, and associated civil and
structural works. Its expertise in Extra High Voltage (110 kV and above) transmission and distribution projects, both
overhead and underground, supports critical power infrastructure needs. We has also successfully executed water and
wastewater management projects, including WTPs, STPs, ETPs, and large-scale pipeline networks. Its capability is further
strengthened through the delivery of advanced SCADA and automation systems that enhance real-time control,
operational efficiency, and system reliability.




                                                                                               189
Our integrated EPCC model allows seamless execution across design, engineering, procurement, construction, testing,
and commissioning, ensuring adherence to stringent technical specifications, timelines, and cost parameters. We maintain
an operational footprint across Railway Zones supported by on-ground presence and a widespread network of vendors,
subcontractors, and local partners. This geographic reach enables effective coordination with government agencies,
railway authorities, utilities, and regulatory bodies, facilitating timely execution and adherence to contractual and statutory
compliances.

Our execution portfolio spans railway electrification and traction substation works, railway station redevelopment and
infrastructure projects, 110 kV and above transmission lines, water and wastewater treatment plants, SCADA and
automation systems, and civil and structural works including RCC superstructures and pre-engineered buildings. In
addition, we operate an in-house manufacturing facility equipped to produce HT/LT panels and compact substations with
CPRI type-tested designs. This manufacturing integration enables better quality control, shorter delivery cycles, and
tailored solutions aligned with project-specific requirements, further enhancing its execution efficiency.

Through its multi-disciplinary engineering expertise and integrated execution ecosystem, we are well-positioned to deliver
end-to-end infrastructure solutions with precision, consistency, and reliability across multiple sectors and geographies.

b)   Cost efficiency through in-house panel manufacturing

An in-house manufacturing facility in Karnataka, whe re we manufacture High Tension (HT) and Low Tension (LT)
electrical panels, forms a key component of our cost management and operational strategy. Under LT, we manufacture
both 3-phase 415-volt systems (industry standard) as well as 3-phase 750-volt systems, based on specific project
requirements. In almost all our service projects, approximately 20% of the total project value is attributable to electrical
panels, making panel manufacturing an integral revenue component of our EPC and electrical infrastructure works. Since
our panel production is directly linked to the execution of these projects, our service operations and manufacturing
activities remain closely interdependent, providing us with operational leverage, improved margin control, and enhanced
project execution efficiency.

 By producing panels internally, we are able to reduce dependency on external vendors, manage material and labour costs
more effectively, and improve project-level margin control. This setup allows us to exercise greater oversight over the
entire production cycle from design and procurement to assembly and testing. As a result, we are able to maintain quality
standards, ensure timely deliveries, and make design adjustments based on specific project needs or client requirements.
Our panel manufacturing facility is equipped with tools and infrastructure suitable for precision engineering and is capable



                                                             190
of producing a range of panel types. For more details on the products, please see “(e) Manufacturing of HT / LT
Distribution Panels” on page 201.

The facility is owned and operated by us and is staffed by technicians and engineers. It also includes in-house quality
checks and testing procedures aligned with relevant industry standards. Additionally, we provide in-house warranty
support for the panels manufactured at our facility. This helps ensure accountability, minimizes downtime during project
execution, and supports quicker resolution of technical issues, if any arise. Overall, our panel manufacturing capabilities
not only enhance our technical delivery but also contribute to project cost optimization, scheduling flexibility, and quality
assurance across sectors we serve.

c)    In-house testing and quality assurance

We conduct testing for every project to ensure that each manufactured product meets stringent safety, reliability, and
performance benchmarks. While many regional manufacturers outsource testing or limit it to client-specified
requirements, we carry out all eight prescribed type tests approved by the Central Power Research Institute (“CPRI”),
even when such testing is not contractually required.

This proactive approach reflects our commitment to zero-defect manufacturing and continuous quality enhancement.
Every electrical panel, compact substation, and control assembly manufactured by us conforms not only to statutory
standards but also to our internal quality benchmarks, which are aligned with and often exceed the specifications under
IEC 61439 standards.

Our in-house testing facility, certified by CPRI, Bengaluru, is equipped to perform the following type tests as per
international standards:

By voluntarily conducting all eight CPRI-certified tests, we ensure that each product is validated for thermal endurance,
mechanical strength, dielectric properties, ingress protection, and operational reliability before dispatch.

These multi-level tests enable early detection of defects, enhance field reliability, and guarantee consistent quality across
all manufactured products. Our adherence to IEC 61439-1 and IEC 61439-2 standards, combined with CPRI certification,
positions us among a select group of regional manufacturers with full-spectrum in-house testing capabilities.

This testing process is complemented by in-house warranty support, ensuring immediate post-delivery assistance and
minimizing operational downtime for clients. Together, these measures reinforce our reputation for delivering safe,
compliant, and high-reliability electrical solutions for critical power and infrastructure applications.

d)    Innovation and adoption of advanced technologies

We consistently place innovation at the core of our operational strategy, enabling the Company to maintain a competitive
edge in the engineering, procurement, and construction domain. Our Company proactively integrates a spectrum of


                                                            191
advanced and emerging technologies such as Internet of Things (IoT)–based monitoring systems and Supervisory Control
and Data Acquisition (SCADA) systems, and advanced automation tools across its design, engineering, and execution
functions.

By leveraging these technologies, we enhance engineering precision, improves system design accuracy, optimizes
resource utilization, and supports predictive maintenance and real-time monitoring. The adoption of these digital tools
further contributes to reduced project execution timelines, improved energy efficiency, higher reliability, and strengthened
safety standards.

Our continuous investment in research, digital transformation, smart automation, and process optimisation ensures that it
remains at the forefront of technological advancements and is able to deliver innovative, scalable, and future-ready
engineering solutions to our clients.

e)   Experienced and qualified in-house execution team backed by promoters and senior management expertise

Our Company is led by Promoters and Directors with experience across engineering, infrastructure development, project
execution, procurement, administration, finance and corporate governance. Agrahara Chamaraje Gowda Abhinandan,
Promoter and Managing Director, has approximately eleven years of experience in EPC, railway infrastructure,
SCADA/automation, transmission and distribution and utility projects and has been associated with the business since its
inception, including through the erstwhile partnership firm. Mahadevappa Tejus, Promoter and Whole-time Director, has
over nine years of experience in project execution, procurement management and construction leadership and oversees
project execution and procurement operations. Hosahalli Appagigowda Savitha, Promoter, Chairman and Executive

The Board also includes Anala, Promoter and Non-Executive Director, who brings engineering and industry experience
with exposure to human resource management and organizational development. In addition, certain members of the Board
are designated as Key Managerial Personnel, and our senior management personnel are involved in overseeing core
business functions and operational activities. The combined experience of the Promoters, Directors, Key Managerial
Personnel and senior management supports oversight on strategic, operational, financial and governance matters of our
Company.

For more details on the background and experience of our Promoters and senior management, please see “Our Promoters
