Our Strategies

We intend to capitalize on the expanding infrastructure opportunities in India through a multi-pronged growth strategy
centred around project diversification, technological advancement, operational efficiency, and strategic partnerships.

Our strategic roadmap aims to strengthen our position as a comprehensive Engineering, Procurement, Construction, and
Commissioning (EPCC) solutions provider, capable of executing high-value and technically demanding projects across
power, railways, water, and industrial sectors.

a)   Expansion in Railway Infrastructure, Electrification, and SCADA Automation

We aim to strengthen our presence in the railway electrification and infrastructure segment by executing large-scale
Overhead Electrification (OHE), Traction Sub-Stations (TSS), and signaling and traction works, leveraging the
opportunities created by Government programs such as the Railway Electrification Mission and the Amrit Bharat Station
Scheme. We intend to develop capabilities to undertake complex, multi-disciplinary turnkey railway infrastructure
projects, integrating civil, electrical, signaling, and communication systems. Our expertise in SCADA and automation
technologies will be expanded to deliver digitalized and intelligent solutions for smart railway stations, traction
substations, and integrated command centres.

To further strengthen this segment, we plan to:

•    Participate in government-led station redevelopment and modernization programs;
•    Partner with technology providers to integrate IoT, AI-based analytics, and remote diagnostics in railway systems;
•    Deliver end-to-end digital automation and SCADA-based control systems across railways, power, and water
     infrastructure; and
•    Expand geographically into high-growth railway zones and industrial corridors.


                                                            192
The push toward 100% rail electrification and digital signaling integration is expanding opportunities in OHE systems,
SCADA-enabled substations, and depot construction. As Indian Railways continues to prioritize capacity expansion and
asset modernization, EPC players with capabilities in integrated design, automation, and turnkey execution are well-
positioned to capture value across this growing market.(Source: Ken Report)

b)   Strengthening the Extra High Tension (EHT) Transmission & Distribution Portfolio

We plan to expand our presence in the Extra High Tension (EHT) and High Voltage Transmission & Distribution (T&D)
domain by enhancing our EPC services for substation construction, HT/LT panel installations, and system commissioning.
With India’s rising energy demand and emphasis on grid modernization, renewable integration, and regional power
corridors, significant opportunities are emerging in the EHT sector. We intend to:

•    Undertake EPC contracts for EHT substations and transmission systems under both public and private sector tenders;
•    Leverage our in-house manufacturing of HT/LT panels to reduce lead times and enhance project margins;
•    Integrate SCADA-enabled control systems into T&D projects to deliver intelligent and automated solutions; and
•    Target new markets across industrial clusters and power corridor states where grid expansion is prioritized.

Our combined EPC and in-house manufacturing strengths provide a competitive advantage in delivering large-scale
projects efficiently and cost-effectively.

c)   Diversification into Water and Wastewater Treatment EPCC

We are expanding into the municipal and industrial water and wastewater treatment segment, driven by national programs
such as Jal Jeevan Mission, AMRUT, and Namami Gange. We intend to provide end-to-end turnkey EPCC solutions,
including civil, mechanical, electrical, automation, and commissioning works for water supply and treatment
infrastructure. We are also exploring Public-Private Partnership (PPP) and Build-Operate-Transfer (BOT) models to
develop projects that generate recurring and annuity-based revenue streams.

Key strategic actions include:

•    Targeting integrated water and sewage treatment projects under central and state government missions;
•    Offering Zero Liquid Discharge (ZLD) and energy-efficient treatment solutions to meet sustainability standards; and
•    Leveraging our SCADA and automation capabilities for intelligent water management and resource optimization.

Growing urbanization, industrial expansion, and environmental compliance regulations are expected to drive sustained
demand in this segment, providing long-term growth potential.

d)   Scaling In-House Manufacturing Capabilities

We plan to expand and modernize our HT/LT panel manufacturing facility to strengthen our capacity to serve both internal
EPC projects and third-party clients. Our existing in-house manufacturing unit, located at Hootagalli Industrial Area,
Mysore and comprising two production sheds, serves as the backbone of our engineering and production ecosystem. The
proposed expansion, situated at Industrial Plot No. Q-140, Industrial Estate, Hebbal, Mysore, 570 816, Karnataka, India
aims to upgrade the facility with advanced machinery, enhanced testing infrastructure, automated fabrication systems,
and digital quality-control processes, enabling higher throughput, improved precision, and consistent product reliability.

Our strategy includes:

•    Increasing production capacity for HT/LT panels, control systems, and compact substations;
•    Upgrading our design, testing, and quality assurance infrastructure to align with IEC and BIS international standards;
•    Developing a modular, pre-engineered panel portfolio for faster deployment in large-scale projects; and
•    Expanding third-party panel sales to utilities, industries, and contractors, creating a standalone revenue stream.

By strengthening in-house capabilities, we aim to achieve greater cost efficiency, ensure quality consistency, and enhance
our competitive edge in large EPC project bids.

Our Business Verticals

We operate through five interlinked business segments, each contributing to our integrated infrastructure and engineering
solutions framework. Incorporated with the vision of delivering technically robust and cost-effective engineering
solutions, we offer end-to-end project execution capabilities covering design, engineering, procurement, project
management, construction, installation, testing and commissioning.

Our diversified business verticals include:

(a) Railway Electrification & Infrastructure

Railway Electrification & Infrastructure is one of the core business verticals. We undertake Engineering, Procurement,
Construction and Commissioning (EPCC) works related to the electrification of railway networks and associated
infrastructure, railway infrastructure development works with associated works such foot over bridges, platform extension
and so on. We participate in the modernization and upgradation of existing railway stations and associated facilities as
part of the Indian Railways’ ongoing national initiative to enhance passenger amenities, safety, and operational efficiency.
The projects are primarily executed for the Indian Railways, Public Sector Undertakings, and large infrastructure
contractors engaged in railway development.

Our scope of work under this segment typically includes:

(i) Railway Electrification

 •   Overhead Electrification (OHE) Systems: Design,
     supply, erection, testing and commissioning of 25 kV
     AC traction overhead equipment, including masts,
     portals, cantilevers, droppers, insulators, catenary and
     contact wires, stay assemblies and other related
     fittings. We also undertake modification and
     augmentation works in existing electrified sections to
     enhance reliability and operational performance.

 •   Traction Sub-stations (TSS): Construction and
     commissioning of traction sub-stations and switching
     stations required for conversion and distribution of
     power for railway traction. Our expertise includes
     design of layouts, installation of transformers, circuit breakers, isolators, protection systems, earthing and control
     cabling.

 •   Sectioning and Paralleling Posts (SP/SSP): Execution of sectioning, paralleling and sub-sectioning posts for load
     balancing and operational control in electrified sections, along with SCADA integration for remote monitoring.

 •   Civil and Structural Works: Associated civil works such as foundation construction, cable trenching, equipment
     plinths, mast foundations, control room buildings and structural steel works.

 •   Signalling, Telecommunication and Allied Systems: Provision of interface works related to signalling and
     telecommunication required for safe and efficient operation of electrified railway networks.

(ii) Railway Infrastructure Works




                                                            195
 •   Civil and Structural Works: Construction,
     renovation and retrofitting of station buildings,
     platforms, circulating areas, foot over bridges,
     boundary walls, approach roads, and other
     passenger interface structures. We execute these
     works in accordance with the architectural and
     functional designs approved by the zonal
     railways and the Indian Railway Stations
     Development Corporation (IRSDC) or Rail Land
     Development Authority (RLDA).

 •   Electrical and Illumination Systems: Supply,
     installation and commissioning of internal and
     external electrical systems, high-mast and
     platform lighting, energy-efficient fixtures, and
     power distribution networks including LT/HT
     panels, cabling and earthing.

 •   Mechanical and Public Health Engineering (PHE) Works: Design and execution of water supply, sewage and
     drainage networks, pumping systems, and plumbing installations within station premises.

 •   Passenger Amenities and Facilities: Development of modern passenger facilities such as waiting halls, ticket
     counters, restrooms, information display systems, escalators and elevators, ensuring compliance with safety and
     accessibility norms

 •   Automation and SCADA Integration: Implementation of integrated control and monitoring systems for electrical,
     HVAC, and lighting installations, enhancing energy efficiency and operational control.

 •   Sustainability Features: Incorporation of environment-friendly and energy-efficient design elements such as solar
     power generation systems, LED lighting, and rainwater harvesting, wherever applicable.

We provide complete end-to-end solutions from detailed engineering and design to procurement of material, execution,
and commissioning of the systems. The in-house team comprises experienced engineers and technicians with domain
expertise in railway electrification, enabling adherence to technical standards and safety regulations prescribed by the
Ministry of Railways, Research Designs & Standards Organisation (RDSO), and relevant electrical authorities.

Our railway electrification activities are aligned with the Government of India’s mission to achieve “100% electrification
of the Indian Railways network”. Our participation in this segment enables it to contribute directly to energy efficiency,
reduction in carbon emissions and modernization of national transportation infrastructure. Under Railway Infrastructure
“Amrit Bharat Station Scheme” and other infrastructure modernization programs undertaken by Indian Railways to
upgrade over 1,000 stations across the country. Through its multidisciplinary engineering capabilities, Core4 Engineers
Limited is positioned to undertake complete redevelopment projects covering civil, electrical, mechanical and automation
components, either independently or in collaboration with other infrastructure developers.

We have executed and is executing projects across various railway zones and divisions, involving both greenfield and
brownfield electrification works. Over the years, it has developed capabilities to manage multiple project sites
simultaneously, supported by a network of vendors, skilled manpower, and site management systems ensuring compliance
with quality, safety, and environmental norms.

Our experience in railway infrastructure also extends to associated domains such as power supply systems, distribution
networks, and automation of control operations through Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition (SCADA) systems.

Our involvement in station redevelopment enhances its presence in the broader railway infrastructure ecosystem and
diversifies its revenue base beyond electrification and traction works. Its focus on integrated execution, adherence to
safety standards, and quality-driven project delivery supports its growth within this strategic segment of India’s transport
infrastructure modernization program.

We are capable and reliable EPCC company in the railway electrification domain, capable of executing technically
complex and time-bound projects for public and private sector clients.

(b) Extra High Tension (“EHT”) Transmission and Distribution Systems

We undertake Engineering, Procurement, Construction and Commissioning (EPCC) works for Extra High Tension (EHT)
Transmission and Distribution Systems catering to utilities, industrial clients, and infrastructure developers. Our
operations in this segment encompass the complete spectrum of power evacuation, transmission, and distribution
infrastructure from 11 kV up to 220 kV voltage levels.

Our scope of activities under this vertical generally includes:

 •    Sub-station Engineering and Construction: Design, supply, erection, testing and commissioning of EHT and HT
      sub-stations, including Power Transformers, switchgear, circuit breakers, busbars, control and relay panels,
      instrument transformers, protection and metering systems, earthing and auxiliary installations.

 •    Transmission Line Works: Construction of overhead transmission lines and associated foundations, tower erection,
      stringing and sagging of conductors and earth wires, and installation of optical ground wire (OPGW) as required.

 •    Distribution Systems: Execution of 11 kV / 33 kV distribution networks, ring main units, pole-mounted transformers,
      underground and overhead cabling systems, and associated civil and electrical works.

 •    Augmentation and Modernization Projects: Upgradation of existing transmission and distribution assets, capacity
      enhancement, automation, and integration with Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition (SCADA) systems for
      remote monitoring and control.

 •    Testing, Commissioning and Maintenance: Comprehensive testing, pre-commissioning checks and post-
      commissioning support including routine maintenance, system audits and performance monitoring.

Our experience in this domain supports India’s growing demand for reliable and efficient power infrastructure. With the
Government’s focus on grid strengthening, renewable energy integration and rural electrification under programs such as
Revamped Distribution Sector Scheme (RDSS) and Green Energy Corridors, our technical capability and execution
expertise position it to participate in both greenfield and brownfield power system projects.

The in-house engineering team and manufacturing capability for HT/LT distribution panels enable integrated execution,
better control over quality and timelines, and enhanced value addition for clients. Its track record in completing time-
bound assignments and maintaining operational safety standards contributes to its credibility with utilities, public sector
undertakings, and private developers.

(c)   Water and Wastewater Treatment EPCC

We undertake Engineering, Procurement, Construction and
Commissioning (EPCC) projects in the Water and
Wastewater Treatment sector. We provide end-to-end
solutions for the development of water supply systems,
sewage and effluent treatment plants, pumping stations, and
associated network infrastructure for government bodies,
public sector undertakings, and industrial clients.

Our scope of work in this segment typically includes:

 •    Water Treatment Plants (WTP): Design, supply,
      installation and commissioning of conventional and
      advanced water treatment plants including coagulation,
      flocculation, filtration, disinfection and chemical dosing
      systems.

 •    Sewage Treatment Plants (STP): Execution of sewage and wastewater treatment facilities using technologies such
      as Sequential Batch Reactor (SBR), Moving Bed Biofilm Reactor (MBBR), Activated Sludge Process (ASP) and
      Membrane Bioreactor (MBR), tailored to project requirements and effluent quality norms.

 •    Effluent Treatment Plants (ETP): Development of treatment systems for industrial effluents incorporating physical,
      chemical and biological processes, sludge handling, and recycling systems.

 •    Pumping Stations and Pipelines: Construction and installation of intake wells, raw and clear water pumping stations,
      rising mains, transmission and distribution pipelines including DI, HDPE, MS and RCC lines.

 •    Instrumentation, Control and SCADA Systems: Integration of process automation and Supervisory Control and Data
      Acquisition (SCADA) systems for monitoring of plant performance, flow control, and energy management.

 •    Civil, Electrical and Mechanical Works: Execution of allied civil foundations, structural works, internal and external
      electrification, and mechanical installations such as pumps, blowers, compressors and valves.

We execute these projects on turnkey and EPC basis, providing design engineering, procurement, construction, testing
and commissioning under a single framework. Its multidisciplinary team ensures compliance with environmental, safety
and statutory standards prescribed by the Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB), State Pollution Control Boards
(SPCBs) and other applicable authorities.

Through this business vertical, we contribute to the development of sustainable and efficient water infrastructure that
supports urbanization, industrial growth, and environmental protection. Our participation aligns with key national
initiatives such as the Jal Jeevan Mission, Atal Mission for Rejuvenation and Urban Transformation (AMRUT), and
Namami Gange Programme, which emphasize water supply and wastewater management improvements across India.

Leveraging its engineering expertise and integrated project management capability, we are positioned to execute complex,
multidisciplinary water infrastructure projects from concept to commissioning. The combination of in-house electrical,
mechanical, and automation competencies enhances its ability to deliver comprehensive, technically robust and cost-
effective solutions to clients.

(e)   Composite supply of HT/LT Distribution Panels along with related services:

Our in-house manufacturing facility at Hootagalli Industrial Area, Mysore, Karnataka, enables us to design, engineer, and
manufacture High Tension (HT) and Low Tension (LT) electrical distribution panels for our EPCC projects and external
clients. The facility supports applications across railway electrification, power transmission and distribution, industrial
electrification, and water and wastewater systems. Our manufacturing process includes design, fabrication, assembly,
wiring, testing, and quality inspection, with products built in compliance with IS/IEC 61439, IS 8623, CPRI type-test
requirements, and other applicable standards. Equipped with fabrication and testing infrastructure and supported by a
developed sub-vendor network, the facility provides control over quality and timelines, enhances design flexibility, and
contributes to both project execution and independent revenue generation. These panels are typically provided as a
composite supply along with our installation, testing and commissioning services as part of our integrated project
execution.

Our product portfolio under this segment includes:

HT Panels: Panels designed for voltage ratings up to 33 kV, such as Vacuum Circuit Breaker (VCB) panels, Ring ain
Units (RMU), control and relay panels, and feeder panels. These are engineered for safe and reliable operation of power
distribution systems, ensuring compliance with Indian and international electrical standards.

Types of HT Panels:

1. HT VCB Panel (Vacuum Circuit Breaker Panel)
2. HT SF6 Panel (Sulphur Hexafluoride Circuit Breaker Panel)
3. HT ACB Panel (Air Circuit Breaker Panel)
4. HT Indoor Panel
5. HT Outdoor Panel
6. Ring Main Unit (RMU) Panel
7. Load Break Switch (LBS) Panel
8. Metering Panel
9. Control & Relay Panel (C&R Panel)
10. HT Capacitor Panel
11. HT Bus Coupler Panel
12. HT Transformer Panel

LT Panels: Panels for voltage ratings up to 1.1 kV including Main Distribution Boards (MDB), Power Control Centres
(PCC), Motor Control Centres (MCC), Automatic Power Factor Correction (APFC) panels, Power Quality Restorer and
Synchronizing Panels.

Types of LT Panels:

1. PCC Panel (Power Control Center Panel)
2. MCC Panel (Motor Control Center Panel)
3. APFC Panel (Automatic Power Factor Control Panel)
4. AMF Panel (Automatic Mains Failure Panel)
5. ATS Panel (Automatic Transfer Switch Panel)
6. DG Synchronization Panel
7. LT Kiosk Panel
8. Distribution Panel

  vertical for Core4 Engineers Limited, supporting
  both our EPC projects and direct supply to utilities,
  industrial customers, and infrastructure developers. A
  Compact Substation integrates the Transformer,
  Medium Voltage (MV) Switchgear, and Low Voltage
  (LV) Switchgear into a single factory-assembled,
  fully enclosed, and safety-certified unit. This allows
  efficient power distribution with minimal civil work,
  smaller footprint, and enhanced operational safety.

 Our CSS units are fully engineered and manufactured
 at our in-house facility in Mysuru, Karnataka,
 enabling complete control over design, fabrication,
 assembly, wiring, and testing. The products are
 manufactured as per IEC 62271-202, IEC 61439, and
 relevant BIS standards, and are type-tested at CPRI,
 ensuring compliance, reliability, and long-term
 performance.

 Types of Compact Substations (CSS)

      •   Package Substation (Standard CSS)
      •   Prefabricated Type CSS
      •   Indoor Type CSS
      •   Outdoor Type CSS
      •   Skid Mounted CSS
      •   Pole Mounted CSS
      •   Containerized CSS
      •   Kiosk Type CSS
      •   Ring Main Unit (RMU) Based CSS
      •   Pad Mounted CSS




                                                           202
     •      Customized / Modular CSS

A Compact Substation is delivered as a ready-to-
install, factory-preassembled power distribution unit
consisting of:

HV/MV Switchgear Compartment

 •       SF6 or Vacuum Circuit Breaker (VCB)-based
         RMU
 •       Up to 33 kV, 1250A rating
 •       Optional features include HV metering,
         protection relays, and remote SCADA interface

Transformer Compartment

 •       Oil-type or dry-type transformers up to 4 MVA
 •       OLTC with RTCC and AVR (optional)
 •       Integrated    protection     for   winding/oil
         temperature with automatic tripping of HV gear

LV Switchgear Compartment

 •       Ratings from 250A to 6300A
 •       Options include ACB, MCCB, ATS, LV fuse
         units, and feeder metering
 •       APFC panel, FRTU/DAS integration (optional)
 •       Copper/Aluminium busbars engineered to
         withstand thermal and dynamic stresses

Enclosure & Safety Features

 •       Fabricated from 2–3 mm CRCA or GI steel,
         powder-coated in RAL standard shades
 •       IP54 protection for HV & LV compartments;
         IP23 for transformer bay
 •       Natural ventilation, locking arrangements,
         lifting provisions for crane/forklift
 •       Fully segregated compartments with access-
         controlled lockable doors




Few samples of Type of Panels Manufactured by us          Pictures

PCC Panel (Power Control Centre Panel)

We manufacture PCC panels up to 6300A, certified for
50kA/1 sec short-circuit withstand by CPRI. Designed
for high fault-level zones, these panels integrate
feeders, breakers, protection, and monitoring systems,
ensuring reliable and safe power distribution.

Key features include a robust busbar system,
protection against overloads, short circuits, earth
faults, and undervoltage, along with user-friendly
operation, interlocks, and multiple incomer/bus
coupler configurations.


                                                          203
Few samples of Type of Panels Manufactured by us           Pictures
Motor Control Centre Panel (M.C.C.)

MCC panels are low-voltage switchboard assemblies
designed for centralized control and protection of
multiple motors. They feature a common power bus
with modular compartments housing starters,
breakers, fuses, and disconnects. Equipped with
options like VFDs, PLCs, metering, and HMI
interfaces, MCCs are ideal for industrial and
commercial facilities with high motor loads. Built for
reliability, they offer robust construction, efficient
motor control, and low maintenance with superior
protection components.

Auto Mains Failure Panel (A.M.F.)

Automatic mains failure is an auto changeover in the
event of power failure from mains supply to stand by
generator and generator supply to mains. These are
applicable for medium & low voltage generators, peak
saving operation, load management, standby
operation, AMF operation co-generation (CHP) etc.




Automatic     Power     Factor    Correction     Panel
(A.P.F.C.)

APFC panels are designed to automatically improve
and maintain power factor, helping reduce electricity
costs and avoid penalties from power utilities. Using a
pre-programmed microcontroller, the system senses
reactive load and activates capacitor banks in multiple
stages (4 to 16), maintaining power factor close to 0.99
lag.

These panels are available with contactor-based or
thyristorized switching and are equipped with high-
quality capacitors and series reactors to minimize
harmonics. Custom-designed as per load patterns and
site conditions, APFC panels support both auto and
manual modes and are built for a wide range of kVAr
ratings.




                                                           204
Few samples of Type of Panels Manufactured by us            Pictures
Synchronizing And Auto Load Sharing Panel

Synchronizing Panels are designed to seamlessly
synchronize two or more DG sets with the system by
matching voltage, frequency, and phase. Equipped
with advanced relays and PLC-based controls, these
panels enable automatic synchronization, load sharing,
and load management based on system demand.

Key features include automatic DG start/stop, equal
load distribution, SCADA/automation integration, and
efficient power management without the need to
manually allocate loads. The panels ensure optimal
generator performance, prevent overloading, and
support a compact, easy-to-install design.

PLC and SCADA Panels

CORE4 designs and manufactures PLC and SCADA
panels for advanced automation and process control.
PLC panels provide logic-based control for efficient
and continuous operation of equipment, often
integrated with AC drives for precise motor control.

SCADA systems enable centralized monitoring and
control of multiple processes across facilities, offering
real-time data, improved decision-making, and
enhanced operational efficiency. Together, these
systems support scalable, intelligent automation
solutions for industrial applications.


LT Panel

To control and monitor the main supply at centralized
location with protective switchgears. Similarly,
distribution boards are utilized for control of small
power control provided near load.




Feeder Pillar

Feeder Pillars are robust switchboard assemblies that
provide local isolation and protection for electrical
distribution systems. Positioned at the transformer’s
secondary side, they safeguard cabling and equipment
from faults, ensuring reliable power distribution.

Serving as the first point of switching and protection,
feeder pillars control and monitor electricity flow
across connected loads. Their design allows for easy
local maintenance, minimizing site downtime and
overall operational costs.

 Few samples of Type of Panels Manufactured by us           Pictures
 Electrical Panel

 We design and fabricate high-quality, custom-built
 electrical panels that comply with international
 standards. We also undertake industrial wiring and
 maintenance of electrical equipment, with all
 switchgear designs handled in-house by our expert
 engineering team. Our product range includes Main
 and Sub-Main Distribution Boards, Synchronizing
 Panels, Motor Control Centers (MCC), Lighting
 Control Panels, DOL, Star-Delta, VFD, and Soft
 Starter Panels, Auto-Transformer Panels, Capacitor
 Bank Panels (with or without harmonic filters),
 Isolator Panels, SCADA Control Panels, RTU Panels,
 and Final Distribution Boards. These panels are built
 for efficiency, safety, and performance across diverse
 industrial and commercial applications.



 Remote Terminal Unit (RTU)

 Remote Terminal Units (RTUs) are microprocessor-
 based devices designed to interface field equipment
 with SCADA and distributed control systems. They
 transmit telemetry data and execute control commands
 from the supervisory system to connected assets. Built
 to meet the evolving needs of modern automation, our
 RTUs      incorporate      advanced      communication
 protocols, robust hardware, and flexible integration
 capabilities offering cost-effective, reliable solutions
 for today's utility and industrial control environments.

                                                            207
Pre-Bidding Stage (Before Winning Tender / Bid Submission)

These steps help prepare costing and technical proposals for tender submission.

➢   Receiving of Indent from Project Team

     o    Project team raises indent for materials/services as per tender scope.
     o    If specifications don’t match contract/tender requirements → sent back for reconsideration.

➢   Shortlisting of Materials and Vendors (Technical)

     o    Identify technically compliant vendors.
     o    Vendor registration done for all prospective vendors (with self-attested documents).

➢   Quotation Requests (RFQs)

     o    Float quotation requests to shortlisted vendors (minimum 3 preferred).
     o    Collect quotations for costing purposes.

➢   Comparative Statement Preparation

     o    Prepare comparative analysis of quotations (price, delivery, quality, compliance).

➢   Selection of Vendors for Tender Costing

     o    Evaluate based on delivery time, technical specs, quality, etc.
     o    Finalize costing inputs for bid submission.

Post-Bidding Stage (After Winning Tender / Work Order)

Once we win the tender, procurement process continues for actual execution.

➢   Draft Purchase Order (PO) Preparation

    o    Draft PO prepared based on selected vendors.
    o    Submitted to accounts and audit for review.

➢   Audit Review & Approval

    o    Audit team reviews draft PO.
    o    If observations → sent back for rectification.
    o    Once cleared, PO is approved by accounts department.

➢   Issuance of Purchase Order to Vendor

    o    Final PO sent to vendor.
    o    Vendor’s consent obtained.

➢   Monitoring and Delivery

    o    PO monitored until delivery of goods/services.
    o    Site engineers receive and verify materials.
    o    Goods Receipt Note (GRN) prepared.

➢   Completion of Procurement Cycle

    o    Process continues with invoice submission, verification, and payment (as per accounts).




                                                           208
Process flow chart for Manufacturing process of Distribution Power Control Panels




➢   Receiving Purchase Order (PO)

        The process starts with the receipt of a Purchase Order (PO) from CORE4 Engineers Ltd.

➢   Preparation Stage

        Upon receipt of PO, the team undertakes:


                                                       209
          o    Preparation of Detailed Bill of Materials (BOM)
          o    Production planning
          o    Preparation of drawings for client approval

➢     Drawing Approval

          o    If drawings are not approved, revised drawings are submitted back to the client for re-approval.
          o    If approved, the process moves forward.

➢     Procurement Activities

          The purchase department initiates:

          o    Procurement of materials
          o    Vendor management
          o    Production of enclosure activity begins alongside procurement.

➢     Production Stage

          o    Manufacturing and assembling of switchgears, bus-bar systems, and enclosures are carried out as per the
               approved BOM.
          o    All necessary assembly subsystems and enclosures are delivered to the production team.

➢     Quality Control and Inspection

          o    Once production is complete, finished products are inspected by a third-party agency.
          o    Strict quality control measures are applied, and quality tests are conducted as per the approved Quality
               Assurance Plan (QAP).

➢     Rectification (If required)

          o    If any observations are made by the quality control team, products are sent back for rectification and rework.

➢     Packing and Dispatch

          o    Products cleared from quality control inspection are forwarded for packing and dispatch.
          o    Packing and dispatch are done based on payment confirmation, marking the end of the process.

These tools and portable equipment form the core of our production setup, enabling modular fabrication, quick assembly,

coating, transformer testing, and high-voltage endurance, we collaborate with certified vendors and CPRI-accredited
testing centres.



                                                                                               227
Raw Materials

Our operations involve the manufacturing of HT/LT electrical panels, SCADA panels, compact substations, and control
systems. The principal raw materials and components used in our manufacturing and EPC activities include electrical
conductors, switchgear devices, busbars, sheet-metal enclosures, control instrumentation, automation hardware, and
related fittings.

We procure most materials on site from domestic suppliers depending on the Project Location who are approved vendors
of electrical brands.

We do not maintain long-term supply contracts; instead, we follow a procurement-on-demand model aligned with project
schedules and client specifications. This approach offers flexibility to manage price fluctuations, ensures timely
availability of quality-certified materials, and reduces inventory holding costs. We maintain relationships with a consistent
pool of vendors who supply materials compliant with BIS, IEC, and CPRI testing standards. All incoming materials are
inspected and verified by our internal Quality Control team prior to issue for production or site dispatch.

Our procurement is centrally coordinated through a procurement team, which manages vendor selection, quotation
comparison, purchase orders, and delivery monitoring. Materials are procured based on approved bills of materials
(BOMs) and project-specific technical drawings to ensure uniformity and traceability.

We also monitor:

•     Lead time and vendor performance
•     Batch-wise quality certification and test reports
•     Cost efficiency and adherence to specifications
•     Preventive replacement schedules for high-use items

This structured procurement framework enables uninterrupted supply, efficient working-capital deployment, and
adherence to project timelines.

We procure a wide range of electrical and mechanical components, sheet metal materials, and fittings for both our in-
house manufacturing and EPC project requirements. These raw materials are primarily sourced from local vendors in the
states where the respective projects are being executed, which helps optimize logistics and reduce transportation costs.

Procurement and Inventory Management

We generally do not enter into long-term supply contracts. Instead, we follow a procurement-on-demand model, sourcing
materials based on project schedules and client specifications. For site-specific needs, we combine owned and rented tools
to optimize cost and utilization.


                                                            228
Our procurement framework ensures:

•    Flexibility to adjust to market price and availability changes.
•    Reliability through long-standing vendor relationships with quality-certified suppliers.
•    Cost efficiency through negotiated credit terms and just-in-time inventory practices.

Our customers

Our customers comprise a diversified mix of government and public sector entities, private sector enterprises, and large
EPC and infrastructure contractors. We cater to clients across railways, urban infrastructure, water and wastewater
management, power distribution, smart infrastructure, industrial utilities, and renewable energy. This diversified customer
base enables us to participate in projects of varying scale and complexity across multiple sectors, while reducing
dependence on any single customer segment.

1.   Government and Public Sector Customers

A significant portion of our business is derived from government and public sector entities, where we participate through
EPC, turnkey, and package-based contracts. Our key government and public sector customers include:

•    Indian Railways – including South Western, Southern, South Central, Western, East Coast, North Western, Northern,
     South East Central and Central Railway zones, for electrical infrastructure, power distribution, and related works.
•    Municipal Corporations and Urban Local Bodies – for sewage treatment plants (STPs), water supply systems,
     pumping stations, and distribution networks.
•    Public Health and Water Supply Departments – for drinking water treatment plants, wastewater treatment facilities,
     and associated pumping and transmission infrastructure.
•    Electricity Boards and DISCOMs – for power distribution and transmission infrastructure, including substations,
     switchgear, and electrical panels.
•    Public Sector Undertakings (PSUs) – such as Rail Vikas Nigam Limited (RVNL), RITES Limited, and similar
     entities, for EPC and electrical infrastructure projects.

2.   Private Sector Customers

We also serve a range of private sector customers across industrial, commercial, and infrastructure segments.

These include:

•    Industries and Manufacturing Facilities – requiring effluent treatment plants (ETPs), zero liquid discharge (ZLD)
     systems, captive power distribution, automation, and electrical infrastructure.
•    Hospitals, IT Parks, and Commercial Establishments – for water and wastewater management solutions, electrical
     panels, and backup power distribution systems.
•    Private Power and Renewable Energy Developers – for substations, electrical panels, balance-of-plant works, and
     EPC support services.

Utilities

Power Supply: Electricity at the manufacturing facility, registered office & warehouse is supplied by Chamundeshwari
Electricity Supply Company Limited.

Water Supply: Water at the manufacturing facility is sourced from the Karnataka Industrial Area Development Board.
Water at the registered office is supplied by Mysore Metropolitan Corporation.

The registered office is equipped with necessary infrastructure and utilities, including internet services, fixed-line and
broadband connectivity obtained from Airtel, as well as computer systems, communication facilities and other office
equipment required for efficient functioning.

At the manufacturing facility, internet and connectivity services are provided by BBNL – Bangalore Broadband Network
Private Limited. These utilities support our operational and administrative requirements and are maintained through
arrangements with third-party service providers.

Marketing



                                                            229
Our marketing strategies are focused on strengthening market presence, increasing lead conversion, and building long-
term partnerships across both public and private sectors. We follow a multi-channel approach that combines digital
outreach, direct marketing, technical consultation, and competitive bidding, ensuring sustainable growth and visibility in
the EPC space.

A key component of our business development efforts is participation in government and institutional tendering processes.
Our team actively monitors opportunities through e-procurement portals and tender aggregators, evaluates technical and
financial requirements, and prepares competitive, compliant, and value-engineered proposals. This enables us to
effectively target PPP, EPC, and turnkey infrastructure projects. In parallel, we engage with potential clients in both
government and private sectors by responding to Requests for Quotations (RFQs) and submitting tailored proposals,
ensuring a steady order pipeline and credibility with procurement teams.

Relationship-building forms another cornerstone of our marketing approach. We place emphasis on timely project
execution, post-sales support, and continuous client engagement, supported by a feedback-driven approach that
strengthens customer satisfaction. This client-centric focus fosters repeat business and referrals, particularly in
government, PSU, and utility projects where trust and reliability are key.

Looking ahead, we aim to reinforce the our brand through technical brochures, case studies, and client testimonials, and
by actively participating in industry events, expos, and technical seminars to enhance visibility within the infrastructure
and engineering ecosystem. Over time, we plan to expand our digital marketing initiatives, leveraging SEO, LinkedIn
outreach, and targeted email campaigns to build thought leadership and connect directly with decision-makers,
consultants, and project developers.

Logistics

We own one truck, which is primarily used for intra-state logistics. Other than this, we do not own trucks, containers, or
other commercial vehicles and largely rely on third-party logistics service providers for transportation of materials,
equipment, and finished products to project sites and customers.

Our logistics framework is designed to ensure the timely and efficient movement of raw materials, equipment, and finished
assemblies across project sites and customer locations. We follow a cost-optimized logistics approach that is closely
integrated with our procurement schedules, manufacturing timelines, and project execution requirements to ensure on-
time delivery with minimal disruption. Depending on the size, location, and urgency of a project, we engage experienced
third-party transporters capable of handling heavy, oversized, and sensitive electrical and infrastructure equipment.

For government, PSU, and large EPC projects, logistics planning is undertaken at both the bidding and execution stages
to align with contractual delivery milestones, site readiness, and applicable statutory requirements. We coordinate closely
with suppliers, logistics partners, and site teams to manage inbound logistics of raw materials and components as well as
outbound logistics of finished systems and assemblies.

Additionally, our logistics operations are designed to remain flexible to accommodate geographically dispersed projects
and varying site conditions. This flexibility enables us to support multi-location deployments, phased deliveries, and just-
in-time supply models, particularly for large-scale infrastructure and utility projects.

Sales and Distribution

Our sales and distribution framework forms a critical component of our business model, enabling the delivery of
engineering and infrastructure solutions to a diverse customer base across multiple sectors and geographies. Our structured
approach primarily caters to domestic markets, with a focus on government entities, public sector undertakings (PSUs),
utilities, industrial clients, and private enterprises, ensuring efficient delivery of EPC services and manufactured products
while strengthening our market presence.

As an EPC solutions provider, we execute integrated infrastructure projects in power distribution, water and wastewater
treatment, smart automation, and turnkey utility systems. Our customer base includes municipal corporations, state
utilities, electricity boards, railways, central and state PSUs, as well as private industrial and commercial enterprises.
Through these projects, we have established strong, long-term relationships with clients who rely on us for quality,
compliance, and timely execution.

In addition to EPC services, we operate an in-house manufacturing facility for HT/LT electric panels and compact
substations, supplying utilities, industrial units, EPC contractors, and project developers. This dual focus EPC contracting
and product manufacturing strengthens our sales channels and allows us to cater to both project-driven demand and
product-specific orders.

                                                            230
Our sales and distribution network is supported by:

•   Direct Project Sales – engaging government departments, PSUs, and private enterprises through tenders, contracts,
    and through Joint Ventures.

•   Channel and Sub-contracting Partners – including contractors, system integrators, project developers, and larger
    EPC contractors with whom we collaborate to supply electric panels and substation solutions, as well as to provide
    specialized execution capabilities in electrical, water treatment, and automation works for their projects.

We maintain temporary set up for project teams, enabling closer client engagement and efficient service delivery across
multiple states. This decentralized presence allows better management of on-site requirements, regulatory compliance,
and customer service. Our sales mix is diversified across government, industrial, and infrastructure sectors, minimizing
dependence on any single client or geography. While government and PSU clients account for a significant portion of
EPC revenues, private industrial and commercial projects provide consistent demand for both EPC services and
manufactured panels.

Through this multi-channel sales and distribution strategy, combining direct government and industrial contracts, channel
partnerships, and manufacturing-driven sales, we ensure our solutions remain accessible to a wide and growing customer
base. Our focus remains on expanding market presence, building long-term relationships, and driving sustainable growth
across the infrastructure and engineering ecosystem.

Infrastructure Industry Growth Drivers

India’s Railway EPC Market:

Increased Government Budget Pushing for Railway Network Expansion: Ministry of Railways plans to invest INR
16.7 lakh crore by 2031 toward freight corridors, electrification, high-speed rail lines, and the redevelopment of over
1,300 stations (Source: Economic Times). These efforts are being coordinated under the PM Gati Shakti National Master
Plan, which has identified 434 railway projects across key logistics corridors (Source: Press Information Bureau Research
Unit). This increases the EPC opportunities for players across the market. The planned investments and infrastructure
expansion are driving demand for electrification to enable faster, energy-efficient, and sustainable rail operations across
freight corridors, high-speed lines, and redeveloped stations. (Source: Ken Report)

Rising Focus on Specialized Projects increase demand for more contractual work: Indian Railways are shifting
towards specialized projects such as tunnelling in difficult terrain, long-span bridges, high-speed corridors, and remote-
region rail links. The government has approved 12 major projects in the region, spanning 777 km with an investment of
INR 69,342 crore. As of March 2025, 278 km has been commissioned, with INR 41,676 crore spent (Source: National
Infrastructure Pipeline). These projects require extensive support infrastructure, including transmission and distribution
systems, overhead electrification (OHE), warehousing, and depots and more creating strong growth opportunities for
component manufacturers and infrastructure contractors. (Source: Ken Report)

Increasing Private Participation through Schemes likes Station Re-development is unlocking EPC Growth: Amrit
Bharat Station Scheme (ABSS) is transforming over 1,300 stations with modern facilities, cultural integration, and urban
connectivity improvements. While initially positioned as a PPP-driven initiative, limited private interest shifted the
execution model towards EPC contracts, creating a pipeline of nearly INR 30,000 crore worth of opportunities for EPC
players over the next two years (Source: ICRA). A select set of stations, including Rani Kamlapati, Pune, and Chennai
Central, are being developed under the PPP model, but the bulk of the scheme relies on EPC. The infusion of private
capital in redevelopment projects further expands opportunities for EPC players, enabling them to capture value in both
execution and ancillary development. (Source: Ken Report)

Urbanization and City Expansion Fueling Rail Infrastructure Demand: India’s urban share is expected to rise from
~30% to 40–50% over the next 20–25 years, with 60+ million-plus cities contributing ~70% of GDP—a shift that
concentrates travel demand and justifies sustained capex in metros, suburban corridors, and station redevelopment. As
large cities densify and Tier-2/3 cities scale up, EPC needs expand across civil works, OHE, and S&T packages for
multimodal hubs and decongestion projects. (Source: Ken Report)

India’s Drinking Water And Waste Water Treatment Market:

Rapid Increase in Policy driven Investments is Driving Growth of Public Water Infrastructure: Policy-driven
investments are accelerating India’s water and wastewater treatment market, boosting demand for private players.


                                                           231
Flagship programs like Jal Jeevan Mission, AMRUT 2.0, and Namami Gange are driving large-scale projects in piped
water supply, STPs, river rejuvenation, and reuse. Urban initiatives such as Delhi’s Yamuna cleanup, Bengaluru’s INR
3,700 crore lake revival, and Vizag’s INR 1,200 crore desalination plant reflect rising investment. New CPCB norms and
reuse policies are pushing adoption of advanced technologies including tertiary treatment, decentralized STPs,
desalination, and smart water systems. (Source: Ken Report)

Government Policies combat Water Stress require appropriate infrastructure: India falls into the “extremely high”
stress bracket, with more than 80% of available renewable water resources already being withdrawn annually placing it
among the most water-stressed nations worldwide. India faces acute urban and industrial water stress, with only 28% of
urban wastewater currently treated, raising serious concerns over scarcity and pollution (Source: Centre for Science and
Environment). To address this, the Government of India has launched major initiatives backed by significant investments
to expand drinking water access, build sewage treatment plants, and promote wastewater recycling. These efforts are
creating strong demand for Engineering, Procurement & Construction (EPC) players to design and execute large-scale
infrastructure such as treatment plants, recycling systems, smart water infrastructure, and pipeline networks. (Source: Ken
Report)

Emergence of Advanced Treatment Technologies drive EPC demand: Adoption of advanced treatment technologies,
membrane bioreactors (MBRs), advanced oxidation processes (AOPs), electrochemical systems and AI/IoT-enabled
digital twins is accelerating as government and industrial actors upgrade facilities to meet tighter reuse and discharge
standards. Further, this is accelerating demand across the Drinking Water & Wastewater Treatment market for advanced
treatment assets and its EPC. (Source: Ken Report)

Stringent Environmental & Public Health Regulations: There is a persistent gap between sewage generated and treated
across urban centers, driving regulatory urgency for new and upgraded STPs and ETPs. In response, state agencies and
ULBs are accelerating project execution under AMRUT 2.0, which mandates SCADA-based monitoring and advanced
automation in approved sewerage works. Simultaneously, updated OCEMS norms for real-time effluent tracking are
pushing industries toward technology-led compliance—broadening EPC demand across civil, electro-mechanical, and
automation packages. (Source: Central Pollution Control Board) (Source: Ken Report)

Aging Infrastructure & Need for Upgrades: Legacy networks and under-capacity plants are being overhauled through
mission funding: under AMRUT 2.0, approved projects already propose 4,814 MLD of new STP capacity, alongside city-
level reforms targeting NRW <20%—both of which require pipeline rehabilitation, DMA creation, pressure management,
energy-efficient pumping, and SCADA integration. (Source: Ken Report)

India’s Transmission And Distribution Market:

Rising Power Demand & Industrial Load Growth Driving Network Expansion: India’s electricity demand continues
to surge, with peak demand touching 250 GW in FY 2024–25 and expected to reach nearly 270 GW by FY 2026, driven
by industrial expansion, data centers, and urbanization (Source: Ministry of Power). This load growth is prompting utilities
to expand 400 kV and 765 kV networks, strengthen substations, and develop new interconnection corridors. Public utilities
like POWERGRID and private developers such as Adani Energy Solutions are scaling up capital expenditure to meet this
demand, creating a sustained pipeline for transmission EPC firms (Source: Adani Energy Solutions). (Source: Ken Report)

Technology Shift and Reconductoring Enabling Faster Capacity Addition: Right-of-way constraints and urban
congestion are leading utilities to adopt High-Temperature Low-Sag (HTLS) reconductoring and compact tower
technologies to boost corridor capacity without building new lines (Source: CEA). This shift favors EPC firms equipped
for live-line upgrades, bay expansions, and compact tower deployment, adding a specialized niche within India’s
transmission modernization program (Source: IEEMA). (Source: Ken Report)

Electric Mobility Expansion Accelerating Urban Distribution Reinforcement: India’s transition to e-mobility is
adding new layers of demand to urban power networks. The rollout of the PM E-DRIVE program, providing dedicated
funding for public charging infrastructure, is accelerating the creation of EV corridors across major cities and highways.
DISCOMs such as DHBVN and BESCOM are strengthening 11–33 kV feeders, upgrading distribution transformers, and
adopting smart load management systems to manage evening charging peaks. This transition is generating recurring EPC
opportunities in urban feeder reinforcement, automation, and charging substation deployment (Source: Ministry of
Power). (Source: Ken Report)

India’s Power Distribution Panel And Compact Substation Market

Expanding Access and Grid Upgradation are Driving Demand for HV and LV Power Distribution Panels: A
combination of government schemes, renewable integration, urbanization, automation, and stricter reliability norms is
reshaping India’s power sector. Together, these forces are accelerating the need for HV and LV distribution panels, which

                                                            232
are vital for managing new connections, enhancing grid stability, and enabling modernized power systems. (Source: Ken
Report)

Industrial Expansion Accelerates Demand for HV & LV Distribution Panels: India’s industrial footprint is rapidly
expanding, creating significant downstream demand for power distribution infrastructure. This is translating into higher
electricity requirements within industrial hubs, reinforcing the need for HV and LV distribution panels to ensure reliable,
efficient, and scalable power supply. (Source: Ken Report)

Technological Advancement: With 20.33 crore smart meters sanctioned and 2.41 crore installed as of July 15, 2025,
DISCOMs must upgrade downstream panels, RMUs, protection gear, and compact substations to support AMI/SCADA
integration. RDSS funding explicitly supports SCADA, feeder segregation, and distribution infrastructure, heightening
EPC demand for modern panels and switchgear. Compact Secondary Substations (CSS) factory-assembled, type-tested
units combining MV and LV components are gaining adoption for dense urban and renewable-heavy zones. (Source: Ken
Report)

EV Adoption and Charging Infrastructure Driving Panel Demand: India's electric vehicle market is accelerating,
with electric four-wheelers registering a 15.68% year-on-year growth in FY 2024–25, reaching 115,800 units (Source:
Vahan Dashboard). Simultaneously, public EV charging infrastructure has surged 5X from 2022 to early 2025, growing
from 5,151 stations to 29,277, at a ~78.5% CAGR over three years (Source: Ministry of Heavy Industries). The combined
rise of EV adoption and charging infrastructure is increasing load demand in urban centers, transport depots, and
commercial facilities, fueling the need for robust HV and LV distribution panels to ensure safe and reliable power supply.
(Source: Ken Report)

Distribution Reforms and Substation Capacity Enhancement: The Revamped Distribution Sector Scheme (RDSS),
launched by the Government of India, has a key focus of strengthening and augmenting substation capacity, alongside
modernization of distribution networks to reduce AT&C losses and improve reliability (Source: Ministry of Power).
Within this push, technologies such as Compact Substations (CSS) are gaining traction as utilities look for space-efficient
and modular solutions that can be deployed in dense urban areas and rapidly growing industrial zones. The emphasis on
capacity enhancement under RDSS is expected to directly spur demand for HV and LV panels, as well as allied equipment
such as CSS. (Source: Ken Report)

India’s Scada and Automation Systems Market:

Policies are Driving SCADA Integration in India’s Utility and Industrial Sectors: India’s push for SCADA
integration is being led by key policies like the Smart Cities Mission, AMRUT 2.0, and the Revamped Distribution Sector
Scheme (RDSS). These initiatives are embedding SCADA into urban infrastructure to improve reliability, efficiency, and
real-time control. In Smart Cities, SCADA powers Integrated Command and Control Centers (ICCCs) for monitoring
utilities like water, power, and traffic. AMRUT 2.0 mandates SCADA for water network management and leak detection.
Further, RDSS projects like in Noida have earmarked INR 396 crore for SCADA-backed grid automation. As utilities
expand, SCADA systems are becoming vital for deployment in dense urban areas. On the industrial front, sectors like
steel, cement, and chemicals are adopting SCADA for automation, energy efficiency, and predictive maintenance aligning
with India’s digitalization goals. (Source: Ken Report)

Remote / Unmanned Operations Drives Demand: India’s utilities are shifting to remote-controlled and unmanned
substations to cut downtime and manpower costs. CEA’s technical standards and the RDSS scheme promote centralized
SCADA/DMS control and automation of field assets, with grant support up to 90% for such projects. State utilities like
Andhra Pradesh and Gujarat have begun converting substations to fully remote operation, creating sustained EPC demand
for control systems, sensors, and secure communication networks. (Source: Ministry of Power). (Source: Ken Report)

IoT and AI as Enablers of SCADA Growth in India: The use of IoT and AI is gradually expanding in SCADA and
automation systems across India. These technologies are being applied to improve monitoring, control, and maintenance
in both urban infrastructure and industrial operations. Companies such as Tata Steel and Bharat Forge have started using
AI for tasks like predictive maintenance and process optimization. As more industries explore these tools, AI is expected
to become a standard part of SCADA systems for improving operational efficiency and reliability. (Source: Ken Report)

Environmental, Health and Safety

Considering the nature of our activities, which primarily involve assembly of electrical panels, the safety framework
implemented by us is commensurate with the associated risk levels. Basic safety measures are followed at all locations,
and essential Personal Protective Equipment (PPE), such as safety helmets and protective gloves, is provided and
mandatorily used by personnel engaged in assembly and related activities. These measures are intended to ensure
protection against routine operational risks involved in panel assembly work. Site-level safety compliance is overseen by

                                                           233
the site in-charge or supervisory personnel, who ensure adherence to standard operating procedures, conduct periodic
safety briefings, and monitor safe work practices.

Competition

Our Company operates in a competitive and fragmented industry, which includes a combination of large, mid-sized, and
regional players. Competition is based on several factors such as pricing, technical capabilities, execution capacity, past
performance, safety practices, and geographic coverage.

The following companies are active in the higher-value infrastructure and utility project segments and have established
presence in relevant markets:

Trimurthi Hitech Company Private Limited: Incorporated in 1989, the company operates as an electrification contractor
with execution exposure concentrated in Indian Railways. Its revenue model is primarily project-based contracting for
railway electrification packages and allied electrical works. The operating portfolio includes overhead electrification and
commissioning of substations/switching stations, cabling, and allied electrification works, with project experience
referenced for Southern Railway. (Source: Ken Report)

SN Enviro-Tech Private Limited: The company is an EPC service provider in water and wastewater infrastructure space.
Its revenue model is anchored in engineering, procurement and construction contracts for public/industrial water systems,
including sewage and effluent treatment projects. The portfolio includes EPC delivery of water & sewage treatment plants
and industrial effluent treatment plants, alongside associated civil and systems execution as part of turnkey project scopes.
(Source: Ken Report)

K2 Infragen Limited: Incorporated in 2015, it operates as an integrated EPC and core infrastructure player with multi-
state execution exposure. Its revenue model is diversified across EPC contract revenues and services/project structuring
& execution support. The portfolio covers end-to-end execution (design to commissioning) across water supply projects,
railway projects, road projects, civil construction works, and related infrastructure builds, with delivery spanning multiple
Indian states. (Source: Ken Report)

Capacity and capacity utilization

We provide a composite supply of services along with electrical panels, which primarily involves assembly and integration
activities to deliver the final output. Accordingly, our operations are not in the nature of a manufacturing process with a

applicable to us.

Corporate Social Responsibility

Pursuant to the provisions of Section 135 of the Companies Act, 2013 and the rules framed thereunder, Corporate Social
Responsibility (“CSR”) became applicable to us from Fiscal 2026, based on the financial performance of Fiscal 2025.
Accordingly, we have constituted a CSR Committee and adopted a CSR Policy in compliance with the applicable
requirements. Our CSR Policy provides the framework for undertaking CSR initiatives in areas prescribed under Schedule
VII of the Companies Act, 2013, including eradication of hunger, poverty and malnutrition, promotion of healthcare,
education, women empowerment, gender equality, environmental sustainability, and ecological balance, among others.

As CSR provisions were not applicable during Fiscal 2025, no expenditure towards CSR activities was required in that
year. The CSR obligation of the Company will commence from Fiscal 2026, and expenditure will be made in accordance
with the CSR Policy and applicable legal requirements.

                                        KEY REGULATIONS AND POLICIES

Except as otherwise specified in this Draft Red Herring Prospectus, we are subject to several central and state
legislations which regulate substantive and procedural aspects of our business.

Additionally, our operations require sanctions from the concerned authorities, under the relevant Central and State
legislations. The following is an overview of some of the important laws, policies and regulations which are pertinent
to our business.

Taxation statutes such as the Income Tax Act, 1961, Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 and applicable labour
laws, contractual laws, and intellectual property laws as the case may be, apply to us as they do to any other Indian
company. The statements below are based on the current provisions of Indian law, and the judicial and administrative
interpretations thereof, which are subject to change or modification by subsequent legislative, regulatory, administrative
or judicial decisions. The regulations set out below may not be exhaustive and are only intended to provide general
information to Investors and are neither designed nor intended to be a substitute for professional legal advice.

Approvals
